enrichment.affected: Clusters running a 1.29 pre‑release where the scheduler's contextual logging feature was enabled; all pods scheduled by those schedulers experienced slower scheduling.
enrichment.fix: The change removes the costly overhead introduced by contextual logging or optimizes its implementation, restoring normal scheduling latency when the feature is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Schedulers that had contextual logging turned on experienced delayed pod placement, which could increase pod startup times and affect cluster throughput, especially in larger clusters or workloads with high scheduling rates.

bugOrRegression.description: kubeadm: changed the "system:masters" Group in the apiserver-kubelet-client.crt certificate Subject to be "kubeadm:cluster-admins" which is a less privileged Group.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kubeadm: change the "system:masters" Group in the apiserver-kubelet-client.crt certificate Subject to be "kubeadm:cluster-admins" which is a less privileged Group.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm generated the apiserver‑kubelet‑client.crt with the highly privileged "system:masters" group, granting kubelet full cluster‑admin rights and violating least‑privilege principles.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster created or upgraded with kubeadm where the apiserver‑kubelet‑client certificate is (re)generated. The change primarily affects the kubelet's authentication to the API server.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now issues the apiserver‑kubelet‑client certificate with the reduced‑privilege group "kubeadm:cluster-admins" instead of "system:masters".
enrichment.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm gain tighter RBAC boundaries: the kubelet no longer automatically has full cluster‑admin access, reducing the attack surface. Existing clusters may need to rotate the client certificate or update RBAC bindings to recognize the new group.

bugOrRegression.description: kubeadm: supported updating certificate organization during `kubeadm certs renew` operation.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kubeadm: support updating certificate organization during 'kubeadm certs renew'

enrichment.problem: Before this change, `kubeadm certs renew` could not modify the organization (O) field in the cluster certificates, forcing users to keep the original organization or recreate certificates manually, which was cumbersome for compliance or naming updates.
enrichment.affected: Users who manage Kubernetes clusters with kubeadm and need to update the organization attribute in cluster certificates during renewal.
enrichment.fix: The `kubeadm certs renew` command now includes support for updating the certificate organization field, allowing users to specify a new organization when renewing certificates.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now renew certificates while changing the organization name without rebuilding the cluster, simplifying certificate lifecycle management and helping meet compliance or naming requirements.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed stale SMB mount issue when SMB file share is deleted and then unmounted.
bugOrRegression.author: andyzhangx
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: fix: statle smb mount issue when smb file share is deleted and then unmount

enrichment.problem: When an SMB file share was deleted before its volume was unmounted, the mount point could become stale, leading to mount errors and preventing proper cleanup of the volume.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use SMB file share volumes (typically Windows pods using the SMB CSI driver) experienced mount errors after the underlying share was deleted.
enrichment.fix: The code now detects the deletion of an SMB share and correctly clears the stale mount state during the unmount process, ensuring the mount point is removed cleanly.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of SMB volume operations on Windows nodes, preventing mount failures and reducing manual intervention needed to clean up stale mounts.

apiChange.description: Added Windows support for InPlace Pod Vertical Scaling feature.
apiChange.author: fabi200123

enrichment.problem: InPlace Pod Vertical Scaling was not available for Windows pods, preventing Windows workloads from dynamically adjusting CPU/memory without restart.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows containers that need vertical scaling of pod resources; Windows node clusters using the VerticalPodAutoscaler or manual in‑place scaling.
enrichment.fix: Implemented Windows support for the InPlace Pod Vertical Scaling feature, enabling the same in-place resource adjustments on Windows nodes as on Linux.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads can now be vertically scaled in place, improving resource efficiency, reducing downtime, and aligning Windows node behavior with Linux for autoscaling scenarios.

apiChange.description: Added support for projecting `certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1` ClusterTrustBundle objects into pods.
apiChange.author: ahmedtd
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added support for projecting certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1 ClusterTrustBundle objects into pods.

enrichment.problem: Pods could not mount ClusterTrustBundle objects from the certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API, preventing workloads from easily accessing cluster-wide trust anchors for TLS verification.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that needs to consume cluster-wide trust bundles (e.g., custom controllers, sidecars, or applications performing TLS verification) gains the ability to mount them inside pods.
enrichment.fix: Implemented volume projection support for ClusterTrustBundle objects, allowing them to be projected into pods as files.
enrichment.impact: Users can now provide custom trust anchors to containers directly via a projected volume, simplifying secure communication setups and aligning with KEP 3257 for trust anchor sets.

apiChange.description: The `matchLabelKeys/mismatchLabelKeys` feature is introduced to the hard/soft `PodAffinity/PodAntiAffinity`.
apiChange.author: sanposhiho
apiChange.userFacingChange: The matchLabelKeys/mismatchLabelKeys feature is introduced to the hard/soft PodAffinity/PodAntiAffinity.

issueContext.title: Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` (the same one as Pod Topology Spread) to `PodAffinityTerm`
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` to [PodAffinityTerm](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#PodAffinityTerm) (like [we do to Pod Topology Spread](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/3243-respect-pod-topology-spread-after-rolling-upgrades)).

### Why is this needed?

Currently, the scheduler doesn’t treat `Terminating` Pods as removed Pods.
See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105661. Pod Topology Spreading gets imbalanced after Deployment/Replicaset upgrades because of that. So, we introduced `MatchLabelKeys` to Pod Topology Spread (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3243).

In Pod Affinity and Pod Anti Affinity, it gives a negative impact on the scheduling result to take old Pods into account during scheduling (“Old Pods” = Pods from a old deployment); Old pods may result in filtering out Nodes that should have gone to the Scoring phase (in `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`), or giving low scores to Nodes that should have been given higher scores. (in `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`).

/sig scheduling
/kind feature
/assign

enrichment.problem: During deployments and upgrades, existing Pods from previous revisions are still considered by the scheduler when evaluating hard/soft PodAffinity and PodAntiAffinity rules. Because the affinity matching uses all label keys, stale Pods can cause nodes to be incorrectly filtered or scored, leading to suboptimal placement.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses hard (`requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`) or soft (`preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`) pod affinity/anti‑affinity, particularly during deployments or replica set upgrades where old Pods coexist with new ones.
enrichment.fix: Adds `matchLabelKeys` and `mismatchLabelKeys` fields to PodAffinityTerm and PodAntiAffinityTerm. These let users specify which label keys should be considered (or ignored) when matching pods for affinity/anti‑affinity, mirroring the behavior already available for PodTopologySpread.
enrichment.impact: Improves pod placement accuracy, especially during rolling upgrades, by preventing outdated Pods from influencing affinity decisions. This reduces unnecessary node re‑filtering and scoring, leading to more stable deployments and better resource utilization.

apiChange.description: Added a new `ServiceCIDR` type that allows to dynamically configure the cluster range used to allocate `Service ClusterIPs` addresses.
apiChange.author: aojea
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add a new ServiceCIDR type that allows to dynamically configure the cluster range used to allocate Service ClusterIPs addresses

enrichment.problem: Clusters could only configure a single static Service CIDR, preventing dynamic or multiple ranges for Service ClusterIP allocation and limiting IP management in large or multi-tenant environments.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that need multiple or dynamically adjustable Service IP ranges; administrators configuring networking for services.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new ServiceCIDR API type that lets administrators create, update, and delete CIDR ranges used for allocating Service ClusterIP addresses, enabling dynamic and multiple Service CIDRs.
enrichment.impact: Users can now adjust service IP ranges without recreating the cluster, support overlapping or segmented IP pools, and scale services in large or multi-tenant clusters more flexibly.

apiChange.description:
Added `UserNamespacesPodSecurityStandards` feature gate to enable user namespace support for Pod Security Standards.
Enabling this feature will modify all Pod Security Standard rules to allow setting: `spec[.*].securityContext.[runAsNonRoot,runAsUser]`.
This feature gate should only be enabled if all nodes in the cluster support the user namespace feature and have it enabled.
The feature gate will not graduate or be enabled by default in future Kubernetes releases.
apiChange.author: saschagrunert
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added `UserNamespacesPodSecurityStandards` feature gate to enable user namespace support for Pod Security Standards.
Enabling this feature will modify all Pod Security Standard rules to allow setting: `spec[.*].securityContext.[runAsNonRoot,runAsUser]`.
This feature gate should only be enabled if all nodes in the cluster support the user namespace feature and have it enabled.
The feature gate will not graduate or be enabled by default in future Kubernetes releases.

enrichment.problem: Pod Security Standards (PSS) did not support user namespaces, causing policies to reject pods that needed to set runAsUser or runAsNonRoot when clusters use user namespaces.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have node-level user namespace support and want to use Pod Security Standards. Administrators must ensure all nodes support and enable user namespaces before turning on the feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the UserNamespacesPodSecurityStandards feature gate. When enabled, all PSS rules are relaxed to allow the securityContext fields runAsUser and runAsNonRoot, making PSS compatible with user namespace enabled nodes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that enable user namespaces can now enforce PSS without false positives, allowing more flexible security configurations while preserving the intended policy guarantees.

apiChange.description: A new sleep action for the `PreStop` lifecycle hook was added, allowing containers to pause for a specified duration before termination.
apiChange.author: AxeZhan
apiChange.userFacingChange: A new sleep action for the PreStop lifecycle hook is added, allowing containers to pause for a specified duration before termination.

issueContext.title: pod LifecycleHandler should support a `sleep` option
issueContext.body:
Many people use `exec` to run `sleep` in their container.  This works, but it's kludgey and requirtes them to have a sleep binary in the image.  We should offer sleep as a first-class thing.

I hacked up a quick POC.  This is obviopusly incomplete (no tests, no feature gate, poor API docs, etc) but could be a starting point for someone who wants to contribute.  I assume it would have to sit in Alpha for a while to deal with back-rev kubelets, so the sooner it gets in the sooner it van be used.

This might warrant a micro KEP, but that's not something to be afraid of.  Happy to help if someone wants to pick this up.

My hacky POC:

```diff
diff --git a/pkg/apis/core/types.go b/pkg/apis/core/types.go
index fbbecb00d58..67a16fe629c 100644
--- a/pkg/apis/core/types.go
+++ b/pkg/apis/core/types.go
@@ -2316,6 +2316,8 @@ type LifecycleHandler struct {
 	// lifecycle hooks will fail in runtime when tcp handler is specified.
 	// +optional
 	TCPSocket *TCPSocketAction
+	// Sleep pauses further lifecycle progress for a defined time period.
+	Sleep *SleepAction
 }
 
 type GRPCAction struct {
@@ -2353,6 +2355,12 @@ type Lifecycle struct {
 	PreStop *LifecycleHandler
 }
 
+// SleepAction describes an action which simply sleeps.
+type SleepAction struct {
+	// Seconds is the number of seconds to sleep.
+	Seconds int32
+}
+
 // The below types are used by kube_client and api_server.
 
 // ConditionStatus defines conditions of resources
diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go b/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go
index 910c7a42edc..8b56aada182 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/handlers.go
@@ -26,6 +26,7 @@ import (
 	"net/url"
 	"strconv"
 	"strings"
+	"time"
 
 	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
 	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/types"
@@ -86,6 +87,9 @@ func (hr *handlerRunner) Run(ctx context.Context, containerID kubecontainer.Cont
 			klog.V(1).ErrorS(err, "HTTP lifecycle hook for Container in Pod faile

enrichment.problem: Containers could not pause during a PreStop hook without bundling a sleep binary and using an exec command, making the pattern brittle and requiring extra image contents.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that defines a PreStop hook and needs to delay termination, especially workloads that previously relied on `exec` with a sleep command.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a first‑class `SleepAction` for the PreStop lifecycle hook. Users can now specify `preStop: { sleep: { seconds: N } }` in the pod spec, and the kubelet will pause for the requested duration before terminating the container.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies graceful shutdown logic, removes the need for a sleep binary in container images, and makes PreStop behavior more reliable and declarative for any workload that needs a delay before termination.

apiChange.description: `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` type checking now supports CRDs and API extensions types.
apiChange.author: jiahuif
apiChange.userFacingChange: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy Type Checking now supports CRDs and API extensions types.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy type checking did not recognize CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) and API extensions types, leading to potential validation errors or policy bypass when policies referenced those types.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that reference CRDs or API extension resources; administrators writing such policies.
enrichment.fix: The admission control type‑checking logic was extended to include CRD and API extensions schemas, allowing ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to correctly validate objects of those types.

apiChange.description:
'`kube-apiserver`: adds `--authentication-config` flag for reading `AuthenticationConfiguration`

/assign @aramase

apiChange.description: Promoted `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition to `beta`.
apiChange.author: kannon92

apiChange.author: palnabarun

The alpha StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration feature flag must be enabled for --authorization-config to be specified.

issueContext.title: [StructuredAuthorizationConfig] - Implement AuthorizationConfiguration
issueContext.body:
Add a configuration format with specific precedence order and defined failure modes for configuring authorizer chain.

Implements https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3221-structured-authorization-configuration

- [x] create API types for config file, loading helper https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119099
- [x] refactor existing authz structs to transform to authz config API type https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119099
- [x] add kube-apiserver flag to accept the configuration file https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120154

xref: https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/authz-config

/triage accepted
/sig auth

enrichment.problem: Prior to this change, kube-apiserver only supported configuring authorizers via the --authorization-modes flag and webhook-specific flags. There was no way to provide a declarative, structured AuthorizationConfiguration file that defines the authorizer chain with explicit precedence and failure semantics.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that need to configure API server authorization in a declarative way; administrators who want to use the new structured authz configuration format.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the --authorization-config flag, which accepts a file containing an apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1 AuthorizationConfiguration object. The flag is mutually exclusive with the older authorization flags and requires the alpha StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration feature gate to be enabled.
enrichment.impact: Admins can now configure the API server's authorizer chain using a structured, versioned configuration file, improving clarity, reproducibility, and enabling future extensions of authorization configuration without relying on ad‑hoc flag combinations.

When enabled, kube-proxy will not install the DROP rule for invalid conntrack states, which currently breaks users of asymmetric routing.

issueContext.title: kube-proxy: Drop packets in INVALID state drops packets from outside the pod range
issueContext.body:
**What happened**:
When kube-proxy is configured with a cluster-cidr range, it drops packets with an INVALID conntrack state for all sources on the KUBE-FORWARD chain. This is meant to prevent spurious retransmits in long-lived TCP connections to a service IP, but it prevents clusters from having asymmetrical routing on private subnets with services outside of a cluster. 

**What you expected to happen**:
Packets on the KUBE-FORWARD chain with an INVALID conntrack state should be dropped for only sources inside of the cluster-cidr if set.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
N/A

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Change to drop INVALID conntrack packets was in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74840. Backing out that commit and compiling is my current workaround.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.17.2
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
```
NAME="CentOS Linux"
VERSION="7 (Core)"
ID="centos"
ID_LIKE="rhel fedora"
VERSION_ID="7"
PRETTY_NAME="CentOS Linux 7 (Core)"
ANSI_COLOR="0;31"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:centos:centos:7"
HOME_URL="https://www.centos.org/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.centos.org/"

CENTOS_MANTISBT_PROJECT="CentOS-7"
CENTOS_MANTISBT_PROJECT_VERSION="7"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="centos"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="7"
```
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
```Linux 3.10.0-1127.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Tue Mar 31 23:36:51 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux```

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy installs a DROP rule for packets in the INVALID conntrack state on the KUBE-FORWARD chain for all sources. This unintentionally drops traffic from outside the cluster CIDR, breaking clusters that use asymmetric routing (e.g., services on private subnets outside the cluster).
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using kube-proxy in iptables mode with asymmetric routing setups (e.g., private subnets with external services).
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new kube-proxy flag to configure the kernel sysctl nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal. When the flag is enabled, kube-proxy skips adding the DROP rule for INVALID conntrack states, restoring proper packet handling for asymmetric routing.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on asymmetric routing or have services outside the cluster CIDR will no longer lose traffic due to the DROP rule, improving network reliability without requiring manual kernel sysctl changes.

apiChange.description: `PersistentVolumeLastPhaseTransitionTime` is now beta and enabled by default.

issueContext.title: kube-proxy conntrack configuration should support UDP timeouts
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

**KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration** should support UDP conntrack settings. 
**KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration** supports TCP conntrack settings and setting conntrack timeout for UDP connections is currently a manual and tiresome process.

### Why is this needed?

Currently configuring `nf_conntrack_udp_timeout` and `nf_conntrack_udp_timeout_stream` is a manual step, and since we already support **KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration**, we can add **UDPTimeout** and **UDPStreamTimeout** fields. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/029d5189701fab73e450158234a0aa81f659f3c7/pkg/proxy/apis/config/types.go#L78-L92 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120076#issuecomment-1693822046

enrichment.problem: Kube-proxy could only configure TCP conntrack settings; setting UDP conntrack timeouts (nf_conntrack_udp_timeout and nf_conntrack_udp_timeout_stream) required manual sysctl changes, which is error‑prone and cumbersome for users running UDP services.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy with UDP services that need custom conntrack timeout values; administrators who previously had to modify host kernel parameters manually.
enrichment.fix: Added new fields (UDPTimeout and UDPStreamTimeout) to KubeProxyConntrackConfiguration, allowing the UDP conntrack timeout variables to be set via the kube-proxy configuration API.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now declaratively configure UDP conntrack timeouts, reducing manual host configuration, preventing unexpected UDP connection drops, and simplifying cluster provisioning for workloads that rely on long‑lived UDP traffic.

issueContext.title: node.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion is a lie
issueContext.body:
`v1.Node` has a field `.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion`, about which [the API docs](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L5250) say:

```
// KubeProxy Version reported by the node.
KubeProxyVersion string `json:"kubeProxyVersion" protobuf:"bytes,8,opt,name=kubeProxyVersion"`
```

but the field is [set by kubelet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L401), which does not actually know the kube-proxy version:

```
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeletVersion = version.Get().String()
// TODO: kube-proxy might be different version from kubelet in the future
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeProxyVersion = version.Get().String()
```

Not only is it possible that the kube-proxy version is different from the kubelet version, it's also possible that kube-proxy isn't even running on the machine.

This field should be marked as deprecated. Ideally kubelet would stop setting it but that might be considered an API break? If kubelet is going to continue setting it, then the API docs and the kubelet source should both be updated to indicate that the field is just an alias for `kubeletVersion` and does not actually indicate the kube-proxy version, and will be set even if kube-proxy is not running.

(Noticed by @liggitt)

/sig node
/sig network

enrichment.problem: The node.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion field is populated by the kubelet with the kubelet version, even when kube-proxy is a different version or not running, causing misleading version information.
enrichment.affected: All clusters where node status is inspected; specifically nodes where kube-proxy version may differ from kubelet or where kube-proxy is absent.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion feature gate. When enabled, kubelet no longer sets the kubeProxyVersion field, leaving it unset.
enrichment.impact: Consumers of node status (e.g., dashboards, monitoring tools, automation) get accurate information and are not misled by a stale or incorrect proxy version, improving observability and reducing confusion.

apiChange.description: Added `optionalOldSelf` to `x-kubernetes-validations` to support ratcheting CRD schema constraints.
apiChange.author: alexzielenski
apiChange.userFacingChange: Adds `optionalOldSelf` to `x-kubernetes-validations` to support ratcheting CRD schema constraints

enrichment.problem: CRD authors lacked a mechanism to safely tighten validation rules (ratchet constraints) without breaking existing objects, limiting schema evolution.
enrichment.affected: Developers who write CustomResourceDefinitions and users of those CRDs; the change is enforced by the API server during admission validation.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `optionalOldSelf` keyword in `x-kubernetes-validations`, allowing validations to reference the prior version of the object when ratcheting constraints.
enrichment.impact: Enables safe, incremental tightening of CRD validation schemas, preventing accidental rejection of existing resources and improving upgrade experience for CRD users.

apiChange.description:
`kube-proxy` now has a new nftables-based mode, available by running

    `kube-proxy --feature-gates NFTablesProxyMode=true --proxy-mode nftables`

This is currently an alpha-level feature and while it probably will not
eat your data, it may nibble at it a bit. (It passes e2e testing but has
not yet seen real-world use.)

At this point it should be functionally mostly identical to the iptables
mode, except that it does not (and will not) support Service NodePorts on
127.0.0.1. (Also note that there are currently no command-line arguments
for the nftables-specific config; you will need to use a config file if
you want to set the equivalent of any of the `--iptables-xxx` options.)

As this code is still very new, it has not been heavily optimized yet;
while it is expected to _eventually_ have better performance than the
iptables backend, very little performance testing has been done so far.
apiChange.author: danwinship

apiChange.description:
The `flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3` `FlowSchema` and `PriorityLevelConfiguration` APIs has been promoted to `flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1`, with the following changes:
- `PriorityLevelConfiguration`: the `.spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares` field defaults to `30` only if the field is omitted (v1beta3 also defaulted an explicit `0` value to `30`). Specifying an explicit `0` value is not allowed in the `v1` version in v1.29 to ensure compatibility with `v1.28` API servers. In `v1.30`, explicit `0` values will be allowed in this field in the `v1` API.
The `flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3` APIs are deprecated and will no longer be served in v1.32. All existing objects are available via the `v1` APIs. Transition clients and manifests to use the `v1` APIs before upgrading to `v1.32`.
apiChange.author: tkashem
apiChange.userFacingChange:
The flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration APIs has been promoted to flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1, with the following changes:
* PriorityLevelConfiguration: the `.spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares` field defaults to `30` only if the field is omitted (v1beta3 also defaulted an explicit `0` value to `30`). Specifying an explicit `0` value is not allowed in the `v1` version in v1.29 to ensure compatibility with 1.28 API servers. In v1.30, explicit `0` values will be allowed in this field in the `v1` API.
The flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 APIs are deprecated and will no longer be served in v1.32. All existing objects are available via the `v1` APIs. Transition clients and manifests to use the `v1` APIs before upgrading to v1.32.

enrichment.problem: The FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration APIs were only available in v1beta3. When promoted to v1, the handling of `.spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares` changed: an explicit value of 0 is no longer accepted in v1.29 (default of 30 is applied only when the field is omitted). Existing manifests or clients that set `nominalConcurrencyShares: 0` or still use the deprecated v1beta3 API will encounter validation errors or missing resources after upgrade, and v1beta3 will be removed in v1.32.
enrichment.affected: Operators and developers who define FlowSchema or PriorityLevelConfiguration resources, and any pipelines or tooling that generate these objects using the v1beta3 version or set `nominalConcurrencyShares: 0`.
enrichment.fix: Promote the APIs to `flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1` and adjust the defaulting logic so that `nominalConcurrencyShares` defaults to 30 only when omitted. Disallow explicit `0` values in v1.29 (to stay compatible with v1.28) and re‑allow them starting in v1.30. Deprecate the v1beta3 versions and advise users to migrate manifests and client code to the v1 API before upgrading to v1.32.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgraded to v1.29 or later will reject FlowSchema/PriorityLevelConfiguration objects that set `nominalConcurrencyShares: 0` or that still reference the v1beta3 API. Users must update manifests and client libraries to use the v1 API and avoid explicit zero values until v1.30. This prevents upgrade‑time validation failures and ensures consistent flow‑control behavior across versions.

issueContext.title: Fixes in cel-go breaks backward compatible of CRD validation rules between 1.27 and 1.28 release
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We were using cel-go v0.12.7 in Kubernetes 1.27 release and cel-go v0.16.0 in Kubernetes 1.28 release. There are many changes from cel-go side between those two releases and some may break backward compatible of CRD validation rules.

An example would be the estimated cost for CRD validation rules(Thanks to @inteon who brought this to our attention with the following example).
In the example CRD validation rules below:
```
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: resources.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: Resource
    listKind: ResourceList
    plural: resources
    singular: resource
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        properties:
          apiVersion:
            type: string
          kind:
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            items:
              properties:
                a:
                  type: string
                b:
                  type: string
                c:
                  type: string
                d:
                  type: string
                e:
                  type: string
                f:
                  type: string
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-validations:
              - message: must have exactly one field set
                rule: '(has(self.a) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.b) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.c)
                  ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.d) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.e) ? 1 : 0)
                  + (has(self.f) ? 1 : 0) == 1'
            type: array
        type: object
    served: true
    storage: true
    ...
```
It will pass perfect in Kubernetes 1.27 version but fail in Kubernetes 1.28 with error:
`Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of 1.6x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength wher

enrichment.problem: Upgrading a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) could fail because the per‑expression cost limit check for x-kubernetes-validations was applied to all validation rules, even those that hadn’t changed. Changes in cel-go between Kubernetes 1.27 and 1.28 altered cost estimation, causing previously valid rules to exceed the limit and block the CRD update.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators updating CRDs that include x-kubernetes-validations rules, especially during upgrades from Kubernetes 1.27 to 1.28 or later.
enrichment.fix: When a CRD is updated, the apiserver now skips the cost‑limit evaluation for x‑kubernetes‑validations rules belonging to versions that were not mutated. Only rules that were actually changed are re‑checked, restoring backward compatibility.
enrichment.impact: Users can now update CRDs that contain existing CEL validation rules without encountering false cost‑limit rejections. This smooths upgrades between Kubernetes releases and prevents unnecessary roll‑backs or manual rule adjustments.

issueContext.title: kube-controller-manager should not cache managedFields
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Remove [`managedFields`](https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/v0.27.2/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go#L271) from the cached used by controllers in `kube-controller-manager`. If feasible, this work will be applied to other components having similar use patterns but have no use of `managedFields` at all.

### Why is this needed?

Roughly the content in `managedFields` is a copy of whole object so it takes roughly 40% of total object size, which is a significant memory overhead. Removing it for controllers can improve memory efficiency

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager cached the full .metadata.managedFields of each object, which can represent up to ~40% of the object's size, leading to unnecessary memory consumption.
enrichment.affected: Controllers running inside kube-controller-manager that previously cached managedFields fields.
enrichment.fix: The controller manager no longer caches the managedFields field for objects, dropping it from its in‑memory cache.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the memory footprint of kube-controller-manager, improving overall resource efficiency and allowing clusters to run more controllers or workloads on the same hardware.

issueContext.title: API: ResourceRequirements usage in Container and PVC
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The same ResourceRequirements struct is used in two only loosely related entities (Container and PersistentVolumeClaim). Extending ResourceRequirements for dynamic resource requirement had the unintended effect that the new `Claims` field also became available in a PersistentVolumeClaim.



### What did you expect to happen?

Extending one should not affect the other.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#pullrequestreview-1302112278:

> We just ran across this while reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107776
>
> The ResourceRequirements type is also used within the PersistentVolumeSpec type (which is also used indirectly in pod specs via ephemeral volumes), and the "clear if feature-gate is disabled" logic is only wired to podspec-handling. That means in 1.26 PVC objects or PodSpecs with ephemeral volumes defined can persist data in this field even if the feature is disabled.
>
> Can you open a PR to clear this field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update flows, and file a follow-up issue to consider splitting the type used in PVCs so it doesn't continue inheriting work done that is targeted at pods?

TODO:

- [x] clear this field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update flows
- [ ] splitting the type

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

na

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig node

### Kubernetes version

Kubernetes >= 1.26

### Cloud provider

na

### OS version

_No response_

### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

enrichment.problem: The shared ResourceRequirements struct was used for both containers and PersistentVolumeClaims. Extending it added a new Claims field that unintentionally appeared in PVCs and ephemeral volumes, breaking feature‑gate expectations and allowing unsupported data to be persisted.
enrichment.affected: Developers and clusters that create PersistentVolumeClaims or use ephemeral volumes. Users who relied on the old ResourceRequirements struct for volume specifications are affected by the API change.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a dedicated VolumeResourceRequirements struct for volume‑related resources and replace the use of ResourceRequirements with it. Clear the Claims field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update paths, separating container and volume resource specifications.
enrichment.impact: Prevents PVC and volume objects from exposing container‑specific fields, ensuring feature gates work correctly and avoiding misconfiguration or validation errors for users handling storage resources.

issueContext.title: After upgrading to version v1.27.3 `Adding GroupVersion` is repeated in the api-server log
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I upgraded k3s from `v1.26.2+k3s1` to `v1.27.3+k3s1` and noticed a log message `Adding GroupVersion` is repeated in the k3s.log. I also see this message when deploying a container that uses apiserver aggregation, such as `kubevirt` in other distros such as `minikube` in the api-server log.

### What did you expect to happen?

The message should not repeated in the logs.  This causes a nuisance and the logs eventually are rotated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Upgrade kubernetes to `v1.27.3` and install a container that uses uses apiserver aggregation such as `calico` or `kubevirt`.  

### Anything else we need to know?

For reference the original issue was reported here:
https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/8038

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
WARNING: This version information is deprecated and will be replaced with the output from kubectl version --short.  Use --output=yaml|json to get the full version.

Kustomize Version: v5.0.1
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"27", GitVersion:"v1.27.3", GitCommit:"25b4e43193bcda6c7328a6d147b1fb73a33f1598", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2023-06-14T09:47:40Z", GoVersion:"go1.20.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME=Fedora
VERSION="33 (Workstation Edition)"
ID=fedora
VERSION_ID=33
VERSION_CODENAME=""
PLATFORM_ID="platform:f33"

enrichment.problem: The apiserver repeatedly logged "Adding GroupVersion" even when no new GroupVersion was being added, causing log spam.

issueContext.title: Include Preemptor Pod UID in Event by kube-scheduler
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

/sig scheduling

Include the Pod UID in the event message for preemption by kube-scheduler

### Why is this needed?

Minimizes the need for an end user to consult the ops team to learn about what caused their pods to be preempted, without compromising PII.

From https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114882#issuecomment-1670906149

enrichment.problem: The preemption event logs from kube-scheduler no longer included identifying information about the preemptor pod (name and namespace were removed), making it difficult for users to determine which pod caused a preemption without contacting ops.
enrichment.affected: Users relying on preemption events to understand pod scheduling failures; clusters where pods are preempted by the scheduler.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now includes the preemptor pod's UID in the preemption event message, restoring a reliable identifier for debugging while preserving privacy.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can quickly identify the source of a preemption directly from the event log, reducing troubleshooting time and improving transparency without exposing PII.

`scheduler`: handling of unschedulable pods because a `ResourceClass` is missing
is a bit more efficient and no longer relies on periodic retries.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: scheduler: handling of unschedulable pods because a ResourceClass is missing is a bit more efficient and no longer relies on periodic retries

enrichment.problem: When a pod cannot be scheduled because the required ResourceClass does not exist, the scheduler used periodic retries, causing unnecessary load and latency.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request a non‑existent ResourceClass and the scheduler component that processes them.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now detects the missing ResourceClass situation and handles the unschedulable pod more efficiently, eliminating the periodic retry loop.
enrichment.impact: Reduces scheduler CPU usage and API server traffic, leading to faster scheduling decisions and lower resource consumption for clusters that encounter missing ResourceClass errors.

other.description:
`kubeadm`: promoted feature gate `EtcdLearnerMode` to `beta`. Learner mode for
joining `etcd` members is now enabled by default.
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: promoted feature gate `EtcdLearnerMode` to beta. Learner mode for joining etcd members is now enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: When adding new members to an etcd cluster via kubeadm, the members were added as full voting members by default, which can cause extra load and longer disruption during the join process.
enrichment.affected: Clusters created or expanded with kubeadm that add new etcd members. Administrators performing etcd member joins or upgrades using kubeadm are directly affected.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the `EtcdLearnerMode` feature gate to beta and enabled learner mode by default in kubeadm. New etcd members are now added as learners first, syncing state before becoming voting members.
enrichment.impact: Joining new etcd members becomes faster and less disruptive, improving cluster stability and reducing performance impact during scaling or recovery operations. Users no longer need to manually enable the learner mode flag.

other.description: Removed the `GRPCContainerProbe` feature gate (the feature is stable and always enabled).
other.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: The `GRPCContainerProbe` feature gate remained in the codebase even though the feature graduated to stable and is always enabled, leading to potential confusion or configuration errors for users who still set the gate in their kubelet config.
enrichment.affected: Users who have `GRPCContainerProbe` listed in their kubelet feature‑gate configuration. The change does not affect runtime behavior of the probe itself, which remains enabled.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate definition has been removed from the code. The GRPC container probe feature is now permanently enabled and no longer configurable via a feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that explicitly set `GRPCContainerProbe=false` in their kubelet configuration will need to update the config, as the setting is no longer recognized. This streamlines the feature set and reduces configuration complexity for all users.

other.description: Removed the `DownwardAPIHugePages` feature gate (the feature is stable and always enabled)
other.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: The DownwardAPIHugePages feature gate remained in the codebase even though the feature has graduated to stable and is always enabled, leading to unnecessary configuration options and potential confusion for users.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where administrators had enabled or disabled the DownwardAPIHugePages feature gate in the kube-apiserver or kubelet configuration. After removal, the flag must be removed from those configurations.
enrichment.fix: Removed the DownwardAPIHugePages feature gate from the source code and documentation, as the feature is now permanently enabled.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to manage or set the DownwardAPIHugePages flag. Users who previously set the flag must clean up their component configurations, but there are no functional changes to workloads.

other.description:
`kubeadm`: removed `system:masters` organization from `apiserver-etcd-client`
certificate.
other.author: SataQiu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: remove 'system:masters' organization from apiserver-etcd-client certificate

enrichment.problem: kubeadm generated apiserver-etcd-client certificates that included the privileged "system:masters" group, granting unnecessary high privileges to the apiserver's etcd client.
enrichment.affected: Clusters created with kubeadm where the apiserver-etcd-client certificate was used for authentication and any RBAC rules that granted permissions to the "system:masters" group for that client.
enrichment.fix: The certificate generation logic now omits the "system:masters" organization from the apiserver-etcd-client certificate, limiting its permissions to only what is required for etcd communication.

other.description: The metrics controlled by the `ComponentSLIs` feature-gate and served at `/metrics/slis` are now GA and unconditionally enabled. The feature-gate will be removed in `v1.31`.
other.author: logicalhan
other.userFacingChange: The metrics controlled by the ComponentSLIs feature-gate and served at /metrics/slis are now GA and unconditionally enabled. The feature-gate will be removed in 1.31.

enrichment.problem: ComponentSLIs metrics were behind the ComponentSLIs feature‑gate, requiring users to enable the gate to expose /metrics/slis. This added configuration overhead and could lead to missing SLI data for clusters where the gate was not enabled.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster version <1.31 that had the ComponentSLIs feature‑gate disabled, as well as tooling that relied on those metrics being optional. All cluster components that expose /metrics/slis (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, etc.) are now impacted.
enrichment.fix: The ComponentSLIs feature‑gate has been removed and the metrics are now generally available and always enabled. All components now serve SLI metrics at /metrics/slis without any gate.
enrichment.impact: Operators and observability tools can reliably scrape SLI metrics from every component without extra feature‑gate configuration, simplifying monitoring setups and enabling consistent service‑level‑indicator reporting. The only side effect is a slight increase in metrics volume for clusters that previously disabled the gate.

other.description: Set the resolution for the `job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds` metric from `4ms` to `1min`.
other.author: alculquicondor
other.userFacingChange: Set the resolution for the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric from 4ms to 1min

enrichment.problem: The `job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds` metric emitted by the Job controller had a very fine resolution of 4 ms. This high‑resolution bucket caused excessive cardinality and storage overhead for monitoring systems that scrape the metric.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that scrape the Job controller metrics, especially those using Prometheus or other time‑series databases for Job latency monitoring.
enrichment.fix: The metric’s bucket resolution is changed from 4 ms to 1 minute, drastically reducing the number of distinct metric values while still providing useful latency information at a coarser granularity.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring stacks (e.g., Prometheus) collect far fewer data points, lowering storage and query load and improving overall observability performance. Users monitoring Job controller latency see a less granular but more sustainable metric.

other.description: `client-go`: `k8s.io/client-go/tools` events and record packages now have new APIs for specifying a context and logger.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: client-go: k8s.io/client-go/tools events and record packages have new APIs for specifying a context and logger

enrichment.problem: The events and record packages in k8s.io/client-go/tools lacked the ability to accept a context and logger, forcing callers to use global defaults and making it hard to propagate request cancellation or structured logging.
enrichment.affected: Developers building controllers, operators, or any client-go based applications that record events; existing code may need to be updated to use the new APIs for context and logger support.
enrichment.fix: Added new API variants that accept a context.Context and a logr.Logger, allowing callers to control cancellation and provide consistent structured logs when recording events.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, operators, and any applications using client-go can now integrate event recording with their own context propagation and logging infrastructure, improving observability and reliability of event handling.

other.description:
Fixed an issue where the `vsphere` cloud provider would not trust a certificate if:
- The issuer of the certificate was unknown (`x509.UnknownAuthorityError`)
- The requested name did not match the set of authorized names (`x509.HostnameError`)
- The error surfaced after attempting a connection contained one of the substrings: "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority".
other.author: MadhavJivrajani
other.userFacingChange:
Fixes an issue where the vsphere cloud provider will not trust a certificate if:
* The issuer of the certificate is unknown (x509.UnknownAuthorityError)
* The requested name does not match the set of authorized names (x509.HostnameError)
* The error surfaced after attempting a connection contains one of the substrings: "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority"

enrichment.problem: The vSphere cloud provider rejected TLS connections when the presented certificate had an unknown issuer, a hostname mismatch, or when the error message contained "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority", preventing it from trusting otherwise valid certificates.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters configured with the vSphere cloud provider, especially those that use certificates with unknown authorities or hostname mismatches.
enrichment.fix: The cloud provider’s certificate validation logic was updated to correctly handle x509.UnknownAuthorityError, x509.HostnameError, and error strings indicating an untrusted certificate, allowing trusted connections to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using the vSphere cloud provider can now connect to vSphere APIs with certificates that were previously rejected, restoring load‑balancer, volume, and other cloud‑provider functionality and reducing false‑positive connection failures.

issueContext.title: move GetKernelVersion out of `pkg/proxy/ipvs`
issueContext.body:
The ipvs proxy has code to check the kernel version (including a mockable interface), and this has ended up getting used outside of that code; currently in kubelet (`pkg/kubelet/sysctl`) for figuring out what sysctls are available (for pods to request to be set), and in the future in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120354, for figuring out if a certain conntrack hack is needed.

We should move that code somewhere more generic.

/sig network
/cc @aroradaman @cyclinder

enrichment.problem: Kernel version detection logic was tightly coupled to the IPVS proxy implementation (pkg/proxy/ipvs), yet it was being used by other components like kubelet sysctl handling, creating unnecessary dependencies and making future reuse difficult.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet (sysctl handling) and any component that needs kernel version information, such as upcoming conntrack logic. Also the IPVS proxy codebase is refactored.
enrichment.fix: Extracted the GetKernelVersion function from pkg/proxy/ipvs into a generic location so that kubelet and other callers can import it without pulling in IPVS proxy code.
enrichment.impact: Reduces coupling between kube-proxy (IPVS) and other components, enabling cleaner code reuse, easier maintenance, and future features (e.g., conntrack hacks) to rely on a stable kernel-version API.

issueContext.title: scheduler: register default EventsToRegister in only some extension points
issueContext.body:
## What

register default EventsToRegister only for PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins.

Currently, we register default EventsToRegister for all plugins that don't have EnqueueExtension.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L551-L554

## Why

EventsToRegister affects which events the scheduler watches, and when registered events come, the scheduling queue requeue Pods according to them. The queue checks the event can make Pod schedulable or not via QueueingHint from pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins.
Given this fact, plugins that never be registered in pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins don't need to have EventsToRegister. 
And, currently, only PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit affect pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins. Meaning all other plugins' EventsToRegister actually don't affect anything, and to register default EventsToRegister to other plugins could result in watching events in vain, which all of PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins aren't interested in.

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

enrichment.problem: The scheduler registered default EventsToRegister for all plugins without EnqueueExtension, causing it to watch cluster events for plugins that never influence pod schedulability (plugins other than PreEnqueue, PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, Permit). This resulted in unnecessary event subscriptions and extra load on the scheduler and API server.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using custom scheduler plugins that previously had EnqueueExtensions but were not in the listed extension points; the scheduler itself is affected by the reduced event watch set.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler now ignores EnqueueExtensions from plugins outside the PreEnqueue, PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit extension points, so default EventsToRegister are only registered for those plugins.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the number of cluster events the scheduler needs to watch, lowering API server traffic and scheduler processing overhead, leading to more efficient scheduling especially in clusters with many custom plugins.

issueContext.title: Enhance discoverability of user-installed plugins
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?


Extend the kubectl help output with a dynamic section on user-installed plugins, e.g.:

```
User-Installed Plugin Commands:
  convert       The command convert is a plugin installed by the user
  krew          The command krew is a plugin installed by the user
```

### Why is this needed?

Right now, the output of `kubectl` and `kubectl` help is static and does not include dynamic-inclusion of user-installed plugins.

This is inconsistent with the behavior of the auto-completion options, e.g. `kubectl kr<tab>` exposes `kubectl krew` as possible command, while it is omitted by `kubectl` and `kubectl help` (given that the krew plugin manager for kubectl is installed)

enrichment.problem: The `kubectl help` output did not list user‑installed plugin commands, so users could not discover or see basic details for plugins via the help command, even though they were available via tab‑completion.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who have installed plugins; they previously could not see those plugins in `kubectl help` output.
enrichment.fix: `kubectl help` was updated to include a dynamic section showing basic details for subcommands provided by installed plugins, making plugin commands visible alongside built‑in commands.
enrichment.impact: Improves usability and discoverability of kubectl plugins, aligning help output with autocomplete behavior and helping users identify available plugin commands without trial-and-error.

enrichment.problem: The volumebinding scheduler plugins emitted unstructured plain text logs, making it difficult for admins to correlate log messages with specific scheduling actions and troubleshoot volume binding issues.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that rely on the volume binding scheduler plugin (e.g., workloads that require PVC binding during scheduling). Cluster operators and developers will see more detailed logs when volume binding constraints are evaluated.
enrichment.fix: The plugins were migrated to use Kubernetes' contextual logging framework, adding structured fields to log entries (e.g., plugin name, volume, node) while preserving existing log messages.
enrichment.impact: Provides richer, machine‑parseable logs for the volume binding scheduler, improving observability and debugging of pod placement failures related to PersistentVolumeClaims.

feature.description: Added multiplication functionality to `Quantity`.
feature.author: tenzen-y
feature.userFacingChange: Add multiplication functionality to Quantity.

issueContext.title: Provide a multiplication method for the resource.Quantity
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I'd like to add a multiplication method for the resource.Quantity.


### Why is this needed?

Currently, the resource package provides helper methods to calculate Quantity, such as `Add` and `Sub`:

- https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/8d1258da8f386b809d312cdda316366d5612f54e/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L565-L567
- https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/8d1258da8f386b809d312cdda316366d5612f54e/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L582-L584

Batch workloads often replicate the same PodTemplate, and controllers calculate the resources needed for all containers.

In that case, It is inconvenient to call the `Add` function as many times as podTemplate, so I would like to create a helper function for multiplication.

enrichment.problem: The resource.Quantity type lacked a multiplication method, forcing developers to repeatedly call Add for batch workloads that need to compute total resources across many replicas.
enrichment.affected: Developers and controllers that compute aggregate resource requirements (e.g., batch jobs, CronJobs, custom controllers) were forced to use repetitive Add calls.
enrichment.fix: Added a new multiplication function to the resource.Quantity API, enabling direct scaling of a quantity by an integer factor.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies resource calculations for controllers and batch jobs, reducing code complexity and potential for errors when aggregating resources for multiple pods or containers.

issueContext.title: kubectl drain improvements
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

kubedrain has "onPodDeletedOrEvicted" callback that can be used in custom controllers. It would be very helpful if we add more callbacks that can give more granular control over monitoring, like "onPodDeletionOrEvicitionStarted" and "onPodDeletionOrEvictionFailed".

### Why is this needed?

It would help monitor the draining of nodes on a more granular level. Sometimes while draining, if the pod is stuck during the eviction or deletion of node, there is not much information that custom controllers can get from kubedrain, with the above-mentioned callbacks custom controllers will know which pod is evicting or if it failed during the eviction process.

enrichment.problem: Custom controllers extending kubectl lacked granular callbacks during node drain, making it difficult to monitor when pod eviction/deletion starts or fails.
enrichment.affected: Users building custom kubectl extensions or controllers that rely on node drain callbacks; any workflow that drains nodes.
enrichment.fix: Added new node drain helper callbacks `OnPodDeletionOrEvictionStarted` and `OnPodDeletionOrEvictionFailed` for finer‑grained monitoring, and deprecated the older `OnPodDeletedOrEvicted` callback.
enrichment.impact: Extensions and custom controllers can now track pod eviction/deletion progress and failures during node drains, improving observability and handling of drain operations.

issueContext.title: Make net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time a safe sysctl
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time is namespaced and it is used by several java clients for configuring the tcp behaviour. 




### Why is this needed?

1. It would be helpful to be able to configure this for applications without needing to modify the kubelet args. Notable for services with long running connections like elasticsearch   
Notably https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/65213

2.  if kube-proxy is configured in IPVS mode which may kill long running connections if keep alives are not present  so having it readily configurable would be nice

enrichment.problem: Pods could not set the namespaced sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time, preventing applications (e.g., Elasticsearch, Java clients) and IPVS mode from configuring TCP keepalive without modifying kubelet arguments.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that needs to adjust TCP keepalive, especially services like Elasticsearch or workloads running with IPVS proxy mode.
enrichment.fix: kubelet now permits pods to use the net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time sysctl by default (kernel >= 4.5). The sysctl is also allowed in Pod Security Admission baseline and restricted policies starting with v1.29.
enrichment.impact: Applications with long‑running connections can tune TCP keepalive directly via pod spec, improving connection reliability and reducing the need for custom kubelet config. The change is covered by PSA, so it is secure by default.

issueContext.title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.


### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
Any that supports csi migration
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>


### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

enrichment.problem: The volume_zone scheduling plugin only matched beta topology labels on PersistentVolumes with beta labels on Nodes. After CSI migration, nodes may have GA topology labels (topology.kubernetes.io/zone) while PVs still have beta labels (failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone). This mismatch prevented PVs with beta labels from being scheduled onto nodes with GA labels, causing pods using migrated volumes to fail scheduling.
enrichment.affected: PersistentVolumes that have beta topology labels and Nodes that expose GA topology labels, especially in clusters using CSI migration for in‑tree storage drivers.
enrichment.fix: The volume_zone plugin now treats beta topology labels as equivalent to GA labels during scheduling. If the label values are identical, a PV with beta labels can be matched to a node with GA labels, allowing scheduling to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Ensures seamless scheduling of pods that use migrated CSI volumes during the transition from beta to GA topology labels, preventing scheduling failures and reducing operational friction for clusters performing CSI migration.

feature.description:

feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange:
kube-scheduler implements scheduling hints for the NodeAffinity plugin.
The scheduling hints allow the scheduler to only retry scheduling a Pod
that was previously rejected by the NodeAffinity plugin if a new Node or a Node update matches the Pod's node affinity.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler would repeatedly retry scheduling Pods that had been rejected by the NodeAffinity plugin, even when no new Nodes or Node updates could satisfy the Pod's affinity rules, leading to unnecessary scheduling cycles.
enrichment.affected: Pods that specify NodeAffinity constraints and were previously rejected by the NodeAffinity plugin; the scheduler’s retry loop for such Pods.
enrichment.fix: kube-scheduler now uses scheduling hints from the NodeAffinity plugin. The scheduler will only retry a previously rejected Pod when a new Node is added or an existing Node is updated in a way that matches the Pod's node affinity, avoiding useless retries.
enrichment.impact: Reduces scheduler CPU usage and improves scheduling latency for workloads that use NodeAffinity, especially in clusters with frequent node churn or updates. Improves overall cluster efficiency without changing user‑visible behavior.

feature.description: Decoupled `TaintManager` from `NodeLifeCycleController` (KEP-3902).
feature.author: atosatto
feature.userFacingChange: Decouple TaintManager from NodeLifeCycleController (KEP-3902)

enrichment.problem: The TaintManager implementation was tightly coupled to the NodeLifeCycleController, making the codebase harder to maintain, test, and evolve independently.
enrichment.affected: Components that interact with node taints – primarily the NodeLifeCycleController (kube-controller-manager) and the scheduler's pod‑placement logic – benefit from a cleaner separation of concerns. End‑user workloads see no functional change but gain from more reliable platform behaviour.
enrichment.fix: Refactored the code to extract TaintManager into its own component, removing the direct dependency on NodeLifeCycleController. The new design lets each controller manage its own concerns while reusing the shared TaintManager functionality.
enrichment.impact: Improves code modularity, testability, and future extensibility of node‑related logic. It reduces the risk of regressions when changing node lifecycle or scheduling behavior and paves the way for independent evolution of taint handling.

feature.description:
Added a return value to `QueueingHint` to indicate an error. If `QueueingHint` returns an error,
the scheduler logs it and treats the event as a `QueueAfterBackoff` so that
the Pod won't be stuck in the unschedulable pod pool.
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange: QueueingHint got error in its returning value. If QueueingHint returns error, the scheduler logs the error and treats the event as QueueAfterBackoff so that the Pod wouldn't be stuck in the unschedulable pod pool.

enrichment.problem: When QueueingHint encountered an internal error, it did not surface the error, causing the pod to remain in the unschedulable pod pool indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Pods that trigger a QueueingHint error and the scheduler's unschedulable pod handling logic.
enrichment.fix: QueueingHint now returns an error value. The scheduler logs the error and treats the event as QueueAfterBackoff, ensuring the pod is re‑queued instead of being stuck.
enrichment.impact: Pods that previously could get stuck due to QueueingHint failures are now correctly re‑queued, improving scheduler reliability and preventing silent scheduling dead‑ends.

feature.description: Introduced new apiserver metric `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_inqueue_seats`. This metric is analogous to `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_inqueue_requests`, but tracks the total number of seats, as each request can take more than one seat.

enrichment.problem: Existing flow‑control metrics only reported the count of enqueued requests, not the total number of seats those requests consume. Because a request can request multiple seats, operators could not see the true load on the flow‑control queue.

enrichment.fix: Adds a new apiserver metric `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_inqueue_seats` that reports the total seats currently queued, complementing the existing `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_inqueue_requests` metric.
enrichment.impact: Provides more accurate observability of API server flow‑control pressure, enabling better alerting, capacity planning, and troubleshooting of request‑level throttling.

The scheduler gets new statuses Pending, which are used to achieve efficient enqueueing in the scheduling queue.
QueueingHintFn interface gets simplified by introducing a new status Pending - the returning value is changed to have only Queue and QueueSkip. The scheduling queue determines whether it should treat Queue as QueueAfterBackoff or QueueImmediately via the reason why the Pod was rejected.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler’s enqueueing logic used a limited set of status codes, making it difficult to efficiently decide how and when to requeue pods after they were rejected. This could lead to unnecessary back‑off delays or extra processing in the scheduling queue.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the default kube‑scheduler. Workloads that experience frequent pod rejections (e.g., due to resource constraints, affinity mismatches, or other scheduling predicates) will see reduced scheduling latency.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a new `Pending` status and simplify the `QueueingHintFn` interface so it now returns only `Queue` or `QueueSkip`. The scheduling queue inspects the reason a pod was rejected and decides whether to treat the `Queue` hint as `QueueAfterBackoff` or `QueueImmediately`, enabling more precise and efficient enqueueing.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling decisions become faster and consume fewer resources, especially in clusters with high pod churn or many transient rejections. Pods are re‑queued with the appropriate timing, reducing latency and improving overall scheduler throughput.

issueContext.title: kmsv2: add metric for current size of DEK seed cache
issueContext.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111920.

enrichment.problem: Clusters using envelope encryption (KMS v2) had no metric to observe the current size of the data encryption key (DEK) cache, making it difficult to monitor cache health and diagnose performance or memory issues.

feature.description: `kubeadm`: turned on feature gate `MergeCLIArgumentsWithConfig` to merge the config from flag and config file, otherwise, if the flag `--ignore-preflight-errors` is set from the CLI, then the value from config file will be ignored.
feature.author: chendave
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: Turn on FeatureGate `MergeCLIArgumentsWithConfig` to merge the config from flag and config file, otherwise, If the flag `--ignore-preflight-errors` is set from CLI, then the value from config file will be ignored.

enrichment.problem: When the `--ignore-preflight-errors` flag was provided on the command line, kubeadm ignored any corresponding value set in the configuration file, causing users' intended preflight error handling to be lost.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm init` or `kubeadm join` with both a config file and the `--ignore-preflight-errors` CLI flag.
enrichment.fix: Enabled the `MergeCLIArgumentsWithConfig` feature gate in kubeadm so that command‑line flags and configuration‑file settings are merged, preserving the behavior specified in both sources.

feature.author: qingwave
feature.userFacingChange: Calculate restartable init containers resource in pod autoscaler

issueContext.title: HPA: Calculate sidecar container resource in pod autoscaler
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Calculate sidecar containers resource in pod autoscaler.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f874a224a31a5dc5745a0c140d3769bb178f811/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/replica_calculator.go#L424



### Why is this needed?

From 1.28 user could run **Sidecar containers** in `initContainers`, those sidecar containers remain running during the entire life of the Pod, it should be calculated in [pod autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f874a224a31a5dc5745a0c140d3769bb178f811/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/replica_calculator.go#L424).

If missing the sidecar resources, we will get a wrong pod resource utilization.

We should also correct the related Cadvisor metrics.

enrichment.problem: Restartable init containers (sidecar init containers) were not included in pod resource calculations for the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, causing inaccurate utilization metrics and potentially incorrect scaling decisions.
enrichment.affected: Users running sidecar/restartable init containers in Pods with HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) from v1.28 onward.
enrichment.fix: The replica calculator now adds the resource requests/limits of restartable init containers to the pod's total resource usage, and updates related cAdvisor metrics, ensuring HPA accounts for these containers.
enrichment.impact: Autoscaling decisions become more accurate for workloads that use restartable init containers, preventing over‑ or under‑provisioning of pods and improving overall cluster efficiency.

issueContext.title: kubelet get configmap from kube-apiserver and etcd everytime
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

qps of configmap get request is too high in kube-apiserver.

when there are many configmaps in cluster mounted by running pod, the qps of configmap get request will be high and the request will also need to get configmap resource from etcd instead of returned from kube-apiserver cache.

### What did you expect to happen?

DO NOT get configmap from etcd. Get it from cache of kube-apiserver.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. set kubelet configMapAndSecretChangeDetectionStrategy to Cache;
2. set kube-apiserver --v=3
3. create lots of configmaps mount to pods
4. check kube-apiserver metrics `sum(rate(apiserver_request_total{resource="configmaps",verb="GET"}[5m])) by (verb,resource,subresource)` 
5. check kube-apiserver log

### Anything else we need to know?

I have tested it in v1.22.13 and v1.28.0. The logic to set resourceversion=0 seems never be triggered

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
1.22.13, 1.28.0 
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>


### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>

</details>

enrichment.problem: `--sync-frequency` flag was expected to control how often kubelet refreshed ConfigMap and Secret volume data, but when `configMapAndSecretChangeDetectionStrategy` is set to `Cache` it had no effect, leading to unnecessary high GET traffic to the API server and etcd.
enrichment.affected: Pods that mount ConfigMap or Secret volumes on nodes where the kubelet is configured with `configMapAndSecretChangeDetectionStrategy=Cache`. Node operators must use the `node.alpha.kubernetes.io/ttl` annotation to adjust refresh timing.
enrichment.fix: The change makes `--sync-frequency` irrelevant for volumes backed by ConfigMaps or Secrets when using the `Cache` strategy. The refresh interval is now governed solely by the `node.alpha.kubernetes.io/ttl` node annotation.
enrichment.impact: Reduces API server load and improves performance for clusters that mount many ConfigMaps or Secrets, and clarifies the correct way to control update intervals.

feature.description: Fixed `kube-proxy` panicking on exit when the `Node` object changed its `PodCIDR`.
feature.author: pegasas
feature.userFacingChange: kube-proxy don't panic on exit when the Node object changes its PodCIDR

issueContext.title: Improve logging on kube-proxy exit
issueContext.body:
There are some cases when kube-proxy has to exit and restart, in order to do that we panic, but this has the problem that the log output shows a literal "panic" message and engineers, support, customers and automation gets confused, thinking that is a problem when is the expected behavior.

As suggested by @pohly in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/a38b9363ec3f0c10bb6e6ebc47d731d6c88ae03f#r126178773
 , we can replace `panic` by `klog.FlushAndExit` 

/sig network
/help
/kind cleanup

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy would call panic when it exited after the Node object's PodCIDR changed, producing a literal "panic" log entry that confused users, support, and automation into thinking an error occurred.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kube-proxy restarts after a Node's PodCIDR is updated (e.g., after CNI changes or node network reconfiguration).
enrichment.fix: Replaced the panic call with klog.FlushAndExit, so kube-proxy now exits cleanly without triggering a panic and logs a normal termination message.
enrichment.impact: Users no longer see misleading panic logs on normal kube-proxy restarts, reducing false alarms and simplifying troubleshooting and monitoring of network proxy behavior.
