feature.description: Removed `/livez` livezchecks for KMS v1 and v2 to ensure KMS health does not cause `kube-apiserver` restart. KMS health checks are still in place as a healthz and readiness checks.
feature.author: ritazh
feature.userFacingChange: Remove /livez livezchecks for KMS v1 and v2 to ensure KMS health does not cause kube-apiserver restart. KMS health checks are still in place as a healthz and readiness checks.

issueContext.title: kmsv2: consider removing KMS from /livez checks
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
kube-apiserver goes unhealthy and restarts when a kms provider returns PermissionDenied on Encrypt/Decrypt requests. This may happen when the permission to encrypt and decrypt gets revoked.

**What you expected to happen**:
I expected kube-apiserver to stay healthy and return errors on types covered by the kms provider.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Revoke permission to encrypt/decrypt data by a KMS key.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
[Code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ed4c2dbf9211bec3e080488b0fd67a9725759a45/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/encryptionconfig/config.go#L139) just does classic `err != nil` so I think that checking error code here will resolve the issue.

enrichment.problem: When a KMS v1 or v2 provider returned PermissionDenied (e.g., due to revoked encrypt/decrypt permissions), the kube-apiserver's /livez health check failed, marking the API server unhealthy and triggering a restart.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using KMS v1 or v2 for envelope encryption, especially when key permissions are changed or revoked.
enrichment.fix: Removed the KMS health checks from the /livez endpoint while keeping them as regular /healthz and readiness checks, preventing KMS errors from causing the API server to be marked unhealthy.
enrichment.impact: Stops unnecessary kube-apiserver restarts caused by KMS permission issues, improving cluster stability and availability for users relying on envelope encryption.

feature.description: Added support for split image filesystem in kubelet.
feature.author: kannon92
feature.userFacingChange: KEP-4191- add support for split image filesystem in kubelet

enrichment.problem: Kubelet could not operate when container images were stored on a split (separate) filesystem, limiting deployments that place image data on distinct mount points.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet that need to store container image layers on a separate filesystem or dedicated storage volume.
enrichment.fix: Added support in the kubelet for a split image filesystem layout, allowing it to locate and use image layers that reside on a different mounted filesystem from the primary rootfs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use alternative storage configurations for container images (e.g., dedicated image volumes, separate disks), improving storage flexibility and enabling use cases such as high‑performance or quota‑managed image stores without requiring a monolithic filesystem.

feature.description: Sidecar termination is now serialized and each sidecar container will receive a `SIGTERM` after all main containers and later starting sidecar containers have terminated.
feature.author: tzneal
feature.userFacingChange: Sidecar termination is now serialized and each sidecar container will receive a SIGTERM after all main containers and later starting sidecar containers have terminated.

enrichment.problem: Sidecar containers could be terminated concurrently with main containers, causing race conditions and unpredictable shutdown behavior for workloads that rely on ordered termination.
enrichment.affected: Pods that include one or more sidecar containers, especially those where sidecars depend on the state of main containers during termination.
enrichment.fix: Termination of sidecar containers is now serialized: each sidecar receives a SIGTERM only after all main containers and any later-starting sidecars have already terminated, ensuring ordered shutdown.
enrichment.impact: Provides predictable and graceful shutdown for pods using sidecars, preventing shutdown-related errors and improving reliability of sidecar-dependent workloads.

feature.description: Promoted plugin subcommand resolution feature to `beta`.
feature.author: ardaguclu
feature.userFacingChange: Promotes plugin subcommand resolution feature to beta

enrichment.problem: The plugin subcommand resolution feature was only available as an alpha feature, limiting its stability guarantees and discouraging broader adoption by plugin developers and users.
enrichment.affected: Users and developers of kubectl plugins that implement subcommands; any workflow that invokes plugin subcommands via kubectl.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the plugin subcommand resolution feature to beta, providing a more stable and supported implementation in kubectl.
enrichment.impact: Plugin developers can rely on a stable subcommand resolution mechanism, leading to more robust kubectl plugins and a smoother user experience. Existing plugins gain backward‑compatible improvements without breaking changes.

feature.description: `kube-controller-manager`: The `LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp` feature gate is now `beta` and enabled by default. When enabled, legacy auto-generated service account token secrets are auto-labeled with a `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label if the credentials have not been used in the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year), **and** are referenced from the `.secrets` list of a ServiceAccount object, **and**  are not referenced from pods. This label causes the authentication layer to reject use of the credentials. After being labeled as invalid, if the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year) passes without the credential being used, the secret is automatically deleted. Secrets labeled as invalid which have not been auto-deleted yet can be re-activated by removing the `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label.
feature.author: yt2985
feature.userFacingChange: kube-controller-manager: The `LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp` feature gate is now beta and enabled by default. When enabled, legacy auto-generated service account token secrets are auto-labeled with a `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label if the credentials have not been used in the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year), **and** are referenced from the `.secrets` list of a ServiceAccount object, **and**  are not referenced from pods. This label causes the authentication layer to reject use of the credentials. After being labeled as invalid, if the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year) passes without the credential being used, the secret is automatically deleted. Secrets labeled as invalid which have not been auto-deleted yet can be re-activated by removing the `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label.

enrichment.problem: Legacy auto‑generated ServiceAccount token Secrets are never invalidated or cleaned up, so unused credentials can remain valid indefinitely and be misused.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have legacy auto‑generated ServiceAccount token Secrets, especially those with unused tokens referenced only in ServiceAccount `.secrets` and not in pods.
enrichment.fix: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp feature gate is now beta and enabled by default in kube‑controller‑manager. Unused legacy token Secrets are automatically labeled with `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` after the inactivity period (default 1 year). The authentication layer rejects credentials with this label, and after another inactivity period the Secret is deleted. Removing the label re‑activates the token.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface by revoking stale ServiceAccount credentials and automatically cleaning them up, improving cluster security. Clusters that still rely on old, unused tokens may experience authentication failures until the tokens are rotated or the label is removed.

feature.description: Client-side apply will now use OpenAPI `v3` by default.
feature.author: Jefftree
feature.userFacingChange: Client-side apply will use OpenAPI V3 by default

enrichment.problem: kubectl client-side apply used OpenAPI v2 by default, which lacks support for newer schema features and can lead to inaccurate field validation and merge behavior.
enrichment.affected: All kubectl users who perform client-side `apply` operations, especially those relying on schema‑driven validation and pruning.
enrichment.fix: The client-side apply implementation now defaults to using OpenAPI v3 when communicating with the API server, leveraging the richer schema definitions provided by v3.
enrichment.impact: Users applying manifests with kubectl get more accurate validation and merge semantics, reducing unexpected apply failures and improving compatibility with newer API versions. No functional breakage is expected for clusters that still serve v2, as kubectl will fall back if needed.

feature.description: Certain `requestBody` parameters in the OpenAPI `v3` are now correctly marked as required.
feature.author: Jefftree
feature.userFacingChange: Certain requestBody params in the OpenAPI v3 are correctly marked as required

enrichment.problem: Some requestBody parameters in the Kubernetes OpenAPI v3 specifications were not marked as required, causing generated client code and documentation to treat them as optional.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that rely on the Kubernetes OpenAPI spec (e.g., client code generators, API documentation generators) could have received incorrect required‑field information.
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI v3 definitions have been updated so that the affected requestBody parameters are correctly flagged as required.
enrichment.impact: Improves accuracy of client code generation, API documentation, and request validation, reducing runtime errors for consumers of the Kubernetes API.

feature.description:
`kube-apiserver` added:
- `alpha` support (guarded by the `ServiceAccountTokenJTI` feature gate) for adding a `jti` (JWT ID) claim to service account tokens it issues, adding an `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` audit annotation in audit logs when the tokens are issued, and `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` entry in the extra user info when the token is used to authenticate.
- `alpha` support (guarded by the `ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo` feature gate) for including the node name (and uid, if the node exists) as additional claims in service account tokens it issues which are bound to pods, and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name` and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-uid` extra user info when the token is used to authenticate.
- `alpha` support (guarded by the `ServiceAccountTokenNodeBinding` feature gate) for allowing `TokenRequests` that bind tokens directly to nodes, and (guarded by the ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation feature gate) for validating the node name and uid still exist when the token is used.
feature.author: munnerz
feature.userFacingChange:
* kube-apiserver adds alpha support (guarded by the ServiceAccountTokenJTI feature gate) for adding a `jti` (JWT ID) claim to service account tokens it issues, adding an `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` audit annotation in audit logs when the tokens are issued, and `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` entry in the extra user info when the token is used to authenticate.
* kube-apiserver adds alpha support (guarded by the ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo feature gate) for including the node name (and uid, if the node exists) as additional claims in service account tokens it issues which are bound to pods, and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name` and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-uid` extra user info when the token is used to authenticate.
* kube-apiserver adds alpha support (guarded by the ServiceAccountTokenNodeBinding feature gate) for allowing TokenRequests that bind tokens directly to nodes, and (guarded by the ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation feature gate) for validating the node name and uid still exist when the token is used.

enrichment.problem: Service account tokens lacked optional JWT ID (jti) claims, node identity information, and the ability to bind tokens directly to nodes, making it difficult to uniquely audit token issuance, associate tokens with node context, and enforce node‑specific authentication.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using service account tokens for pod authentication, especially those needing audit traceability or node‑specific token binding.
enrichment.fix: Added alpha support (behind feature gates) in kube‑apiserver to: 1) embed a jti claim and record an `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` audit annotation and extra user info; 2) include node name and uid as claims and expose them via `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name`/`node-uid` user info for pod‑bound tokens; 3) allow TokenRequests that bind tokens directly to nodes and optionally validate node existence at use time.
enrichment.impact: Enables finer‑grained auditing of service account token issuance, improves security by allowing token‑to‑node binding and node identity verification, and provides extra user info for downstream authorizers and admission controllers.

feature.description: `kubeadm`: will now allow deploying a kubelet that is 3 versions older than the version of `kubeadm` (N-3). This aligns with the recent change made by SIG Architecture that extends the support skew between the control plane and kubelets. Tolerate this new kubelet skew for the commands `init`, `join` and `upgrade`. Note that if the `kubeadm` user applies a control plane version that is older than the `kubeadm` version (N-1 maximum) then the skew between the kubelet and control plane would become a maximum of N-2.
feature.author: pacoxu
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: allow deploying a kubelet that is 3 versions older than the version of kubeadm (N-3). This aligns with the recent change made by SIG Architecture that extends the support skew between the control plane and kubelets. Tolerate this new kubelet skew for the commands "init", "join" and "upgrade". Note that if the kubeadm user applies a control plane version that is older than the kubeadm version (N-1 maximum) then the skew between the kubelet and control plane would become a maximum of N-2.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm only accepted kubelet versions up to N-1, so clusters could not be initialized, joined, or upgraded when the kubelet was three minor releases older (N-3), despite SIG Architecture extending the supported control‑plane/kubelet skew to N-3.
enrichment.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to bootstrap or upgrade clusters where the node’s kubelet version is older than the kubeadm version (up to three minor versions).
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now tolerates a kubelet version that is up to three minor releases older than the kubeadm version (N-3) for the init, join, and upgrade commands. It also clarifies the maximum skew when the control‑plane version is older than kubeadm (N-2).
enrichment.impact: Allows clusters to be created or upgraded even when the node’s kubelet lags by up to three versions, reducing version‑skew errors, simplifying upgrade paths, and aligning kubeadm with the new SIG Architecture skew policy.

feature.description: Added a new `--init-only` command line flag to `kube-proxy`. Setting the flag makes `kube-proxy` perform its initial configuration that requires privileged mode, and then exit. The `--init-only` mode is intended to be executed in a privileged init container, so that the main container may run with a stricter `securityContext`.
feature.author: uablrek

issueContext.title: Document and test minimum privileges needed to run kube-proxy
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Running containers in privileged mode is not recommended as privileged containers run with all [linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html) enabled and can access the host's resources. Running containers in privileged mode opens number of security threads such as breakout to underlying host OS.

Currently the kube-proxy DaemonSet runs in privileged mode.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/863a462eeccca4c24bf4c4e9012f5ebccade70a2/cluster/addons/kube-proxy/kube-proxy-ds.yaml#L50-L51

https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy describes how to run kube-proxy in "rootless". To my understanding "rootless" != non-privileged mode but this configuration can be also used for running in non-privileged mode. However I see that following issues with it:
1. In the provided kube-proxy component config in https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy we have to disable certain settins to prevent kube-proxy from ensuring sysctls (which is allowed only in privileged container).

But when I tried to run kube-proxy with the provided component config it fails because it tries to ensure yet another syctl:
```
F0818 08:03:55.514875       1 server.go:494] unable to create proxier: unable to create ipv4 proxier: can't set sysctl net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet to 1: open /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet: read-only file system
```

It is `net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet` that is being set in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58c10aa6eb5adfb1f3aa4d6cb898b8c347ba9e72/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L263-L265

And I don't see a way how to disable kube-proxy from ensuring this sysctl from its component config.

2. In general the whole approach that explicitly sets 0 values to prevent kube-proxy from ensuring syctls seems not a sustainable one. The long lived kube-proxy container should be abl

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy needs privileged mode to set kernel sysctls during startup, forcing the DaemonSet to run the entire proxy container as privileged, which is a security risk and prevents running kube-proxy in stricter security contexts.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that runs kube-proxy in a DaemonSet and wants to reduce container privileges, especially those using security‑focused configurations or rootless setups.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `--init-only` flag. When enabled, kube-proxy performs its privileged initialization (sysctl adjustments, iptables setup, etc.) and then exits. This allows the privileged work to be done in a separate init container while the main kube-proxy container can run with a non‑privileged securityContext.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now drop privileged rights from the long‑running kube-proxy container, reducing attack surface and complying with stricter security policies without losing proxy functionality.

feature.description: Added container filesystem to the `ImageFsInfoResponse`.
feature.author: kannon92
feature.userFacingChange: add container filesystem to the ImageFsInfoResponse.

enrichment.problem: The ImageFsInfoResponse from the CRI runtime only reported the image filesystem usage, so kubelet and monitoring tools could not obtain container filesystem usage data, leading to incomplete node storage metrics.
enrichment.affected: Node agents (kubelet) and any components that consume CRI image filesystem metrics (e.g., monitoring solutions) were missing container filesystem data.
enrichment.fix: Extended the ImageFsInfoResponse protobuf to include a field for the container filesystem, allowing the runtime to return both image and container filesystem usage information.
enrichment.impact: Kubelet can now report full node disk usage (image + container) to metrics pipelines, improving capacity planning, alerting, and troubleshooting of storage pressure on nodes.

feature.description: `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` now preserves types of composition variables, and raises type-related errors early.
feature.author: jiahuif
feature.userFacingChange: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy now preserves types of composition variables, and raise type-related errors early.

issueContext.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Variables field is added to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in 1.28. Currently the usage of variables would expect a operator associated. 
e.g. (thanks to Mariam Fahmy for raising the issue)
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "chech-deployment-labels"
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  variables:
    - name: environment
      expression: "has(object.metadata.labels) && 'env' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['env'] == 'prod'"
  validations:
    - expression: "variables.environment"
      message: "Deployment labels must be env=prod"
```
Above will fail with error: 
```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "chech-deployment-labels" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "variables.environment": must evaluate to bool
```
Meanwhile the `- expression: "variables.environment == true"` will pass.

The reason is when variables be evaluated to non dyn type(like bool or string), it will require special handling(like casting) since we use dyn type everywhere. 

### Why is this needed?

It might confuse user.

enrichment.problem: Variables defined in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy lost their concrete types and were treated as dynamic, causing type‑related validation errors (e.g., a string or boolean variable could not be used directly in a validation expression) and requiring users to add manual casts.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy variables, especially those using non‑bool types (strings, numbers) in validation expressions.
enrichment.fix: The admission API now preserves the original types of composition variables and performs type checking when the policy is compiled, raising type‑related errors early instead of at evaluation time.
enrichment.impact: Users can write policies that reference variables directly without extra casting, get clearer error messages earlier, and avoid unexpected admission failures, improving policy authoring experience and reliability.

feature.description: `CRDValidationRatcheting`: added support for ratcheting `x-kubernetes-validations` in schema.
feature.author: alexzielenski
feature.userFacingChange: CRDValidationRatcheting: Adds support for ratcheting `x-kubernetes-validations` in schema

enrichment.problem: Before this change, CRD schemas could not ratchet (incrementally tighten) the `x-kubernetes-validations` rules. Updating a CRD to add stricter validations required a breaking change, forcing users to either delete existing resources or disable validation, making upgrades painful.
enrichment.affected: Users who define or consume CustomResourceDefinitions with `x-kubernetes-validations` – typically CRD developers and cluster operators upgrading CRDs.
enrichment.fix: Adds support for ratcheting `x-kubernetes-validations` in CRD schemas. New validation rules can be marked as ratcheted, allowing them to be introduced without immediately invalidating existing custom resources, and they become enforced only for newly created or updated objects.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can evolve CRD validation policies safely, reducing downtime and manual migration steps when strengthening data integrity guarantees. Improves upgrade experience for workloads that rely on custom resources.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go `1.21.2`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.21.2

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, which could miss recent language improvements, security patches, and compatibility updates.
enrichment.affected: All users of Kubernetes binaries receive the updated build, but there are no functional changes to workloads or cluster behavior.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.21.2, updating the toolchain used for building the release.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that the released binaries benefit from the latest Go runtime fixes and performance improvements, reducing potential runtime issues and keeping the project up‑to‑date with upstream tooling.

feature.description: `kubelet` now emits a metric for end-to-end pod startup latency, including image pull.
feature.author: ruiwen-zhao
feature.userFacingChange: Kubelet emits a metric for end-to-end pod startup latency including image pull.

enrichment.problem: Cluster operators had no built‑in metric to measure the total time from pod creation to it becoming Running, especially the time spent pulling container images, making it hard to diagnose slow pod start‑ups.
enrichment.affected: Any workload whose pod start time is of interest – e.g., developers, SREs, and monitoring systems watching pods.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now exports a new metric that reports end‑to‑end pod startup latency, and the metric includes the image‑pull phase.
enrichment.impact: Provides operators with direct observability of pod launch performance, enabling alerts, capacity planning, and root‑cause analysis of slow starts.

feature.description: Bumped `distroless-iptables` to `0.3.3` based on Go `1.21.2`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Bump distroless-iptables to 0.3.3 based on Go 1.21.2

enrichment.problem: The distroless-iptables image used in Kubernetes testing was outdated and needed to be updated to incorporate recent fixes and ensure compatibility with Go 1.21.2.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes test suites and CI pipelines that use the distroless-iptables image.
enrichment.fix: Updated the distroless-iptables dependency to version 0.3.3, which is built with Go 1.21.2.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that test environments and any components that rely on the distroless-iptables image run with the latest upstream improvements, reducing potential test flakiness and compatibility issues.

feature.description: Graduated the `ReadWriteOncePod` feature gate to `GA`.
feature.author: chrishenzie
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate the `ReadWriteOncePod` feature gate to GA

enrichment.problem: The ReadWriteOncePod access mode was only available behind a feature gate in beta, requiring clusters to enable the gate before using it and preventing it from being considered a stable, universally supported feature.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that wanted to use ReadWriteOncePod without enabling the beta feature gate, and any workloads (Pods, StatefulSets, etc.) that specify the ReadWriteOncePod access mode for PersistentVolumeClaims.
enrichment.fix: The ReadWriteOncePod feature gate has been graduated to GA, removing the need for an explicit feature gate and making the access mode available by default in all clusters.
enrichment.impact: Users can now rely on the ReadWriteOncePod access mode for exclusive volume use without extra configuration, simplifying storage provisioning and pod scheduling for workloads that need a volume to be used by a single pod at a time.

feature.description: Enabled traces for KMSv2 encrypt/decrypt operations.
feature.author: aramase
feature.userFacingChange: Enable traces for KMSv2 encrypt/decrypt operations.

issueContext.title: encryption-at-rest: Tracing is added to the API server to assess transformation timings
issueContext.body:
This is GA graduation criteria for KMSv2: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3299-kms-v2-improvements#ga

xref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-traces/

- Validate we have the tracing instrumentation to report transformation timings (including gRPC calls)
- Add instrumentation to the PKCS11 reference implementation

enrichment.problem: KMS v2 encrypt/decrypt operations were not instrumented for tracing, preventing users from measuring and diagnosing the latency of encryption-at-rest transformations and gRPC calls.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use KMS v2 for encryption‑at‑rest (e.g., those configuring EncryptionConfiguration with a v2 KMS provider).
enrichment.fix: Added tracing instrumentation to the kube-apiserver for KMS v2 encrypt and decrypt calls, emitting spans that capture transformation timings and underlying gRPC interactions.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now observe and troubleshoot the performance of KMS v2 encryption, meet GA graduation criteria, and improve overall security observability for data‑at‑rest workflows.

feature.description: CRI: image pull per runtime class is now supported.
feature.author: kiashok
feature.userFacingChange: CRI: support image pull per runtime class

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes only allowed a single, node‑wide image pull configuration for all containers, so users could not set different pull behaviours for distinct runtime classes (e.g., sandbox vs. containerd). This limited flexibility for workloads that require separate pull policies per runtime class.
enrichment.affected: Users who run multiple RuntimeClasses on the same node, especially those using Windows nodes or custom runtimes that need distinct image pull behaviour.
enrichment.fix: Add support for specifying image pull settings per RuntimeClass. The kubelet now respects the imagePullPolicy defined in each RuntimeClass when pulling container images via the CRI.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can run multiple RuntimeClasses with independent image pull policies, improving workload isolation, reducing unnecessary image pulls, and aligning with scenarios such as Windows nodes or specialized sandbox runtimes.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go `v1.21.3`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.21.3

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; the release updates the build to use Go 1.21.3.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go compiler.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.21.3 instead of the previous Go version.
enrichment.impact: Provides the latest language security patches and bug fixes, improves build reliability, and ensures continued compatibility, without changing runtime behavior for users.

feature.description: Fixed overriding default `KubeletConfig` fields in drop-in configs if not set.
feature.author: sohankunkerkar
feature.userFacingChange: Fix overriding default KubeletConfig fields in drop-in configs if not set

enrichment.problem: When using drop‑in KubeletConfig files, fields that were left unset in the drop‑in could unintentionally override the default values from the base configuration, leading to unexpected kubelet behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use drop‑in KubeletConfig files to customize node settings; the kubelet on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet configuration merging logic was corrected so that default fields from the base KubeletConfig are preserved unless explicitly set in a drop‑in config.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that rely on drop‑in kubelet configuration now retain the intended default settings, preventing inadvertent configuration changes and improving node stability and predictability.

feature.description: Bumped `distroless-iptables` to `0.4.1` based on Go `1.21.3`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Bump distroless-iptables to 0.4.1 based on Go 1.21.3

enrichment.fix: Update the distroless-iptables dependency to version 0.4.1, rebuilt with Go 1.21.3, and use the new image in the testing suite.

feature.description:
`kubelet` allows pods to use the `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout`, “net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl”
and “net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes“ sysctl by default; Pod Security Admission
allows this sysctl in `v1.29+` versions of the baseline and restricted policies.
feature.author: HirazawaUi
feature.userFacingChange: kubelet allows pods to use the `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout` , “net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl” and “net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes“ sysctl by default; Pod Security admission allows this sysctl in v1.29+ versions of the baseline and restricted policies.

issueContext.title: Add net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout, net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl, net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes as safe sysctl
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add the following to be safe sysctls:

net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout
net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl
net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes

These are related settings to net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time that was enabled in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117873


### Why is this needed?

These are related ipv4 TCP settings for tuning network connections between a client and a pod.

enrichment.problem: Pods could not set the IPv4 TCP sysctls net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout, net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl, and net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes because they were not considered safe, preventing fine‑grained TCP tuning per pod.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that needs custom TCP fin timeout or keepalive settings; clusters running v1.29+ with baseline or restricted PSA policies.
enrichment.fix: kubelet now treats these three sysctls as safe and allows pods to set them by default. Pod Security Admission baseline and restricted policies (v1.29 and later) have been updated to permit these sysctls.
enrichment.impact: Enables workload developers to adjust TCP fin timeout and keepalive behavior for individual pods, improving connection reliability and performance for network‑intensive applications.

feature.description: `DevicePluginCDIDevices` feature has been graduated to `beta` and enabled by default in the kubelet.
feature.author: bart0sh
feature.userFacingChange: DevicePluginCDIDevices feature has been graduated to Beta and enabled by default in the Kubelet

enrichment.problem: The DevicePluginCDIDevices feature was in alpha and disabled by default, requiring users to manually enable the feature gate to use CDI with device plugins.
enrichment.affected: Users who wanted to use CDI-enabled device plugins but had to enable the alpha feature gate; clusters that upgrade will automatically have the feature enabled.
enrichment.fix: The feature has been graduated to beta and is now enabled by default in the kubelet, removing the need for manual feature‑gate configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use CDI device plugin capabilities out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying deployment and increasing reliability of workloads that rely on CDI for device discovery.

feature.description: Introduced the `job_finished_indexes_total` metric for the `BackoffLimitPerIndex` feature.
feature.author: mimowo
feature.userFacingChange: Introduce the job_finished_indexes_total metric for BackoffLimitPerIndex feature

enrichment.problem: Before this change there was no Prometheus metric to report how many indexes of an indexed Job had finished when using the BackoffLimitPerIndex feature, limiting visibility and alerting.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running indexed Jobs that set spec.backoffLimitPerIndex; primarily workload owners and cluster operators.
enrichment.fix: Adds the job_finished_indexes_total metric, which increments for each Job index that reaches a terminal state, providing observability for BackoffLimitPerIndex.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor completion of indexed Job indexes, set alerts, and better understand job progress and failures, improving reliability of workloads using BackoffLimitPerIndex.

feature.description: `kubeadm`: a separate "super-admin.conf" file is now deployed. The User in `admin.conf` is now bound to a new RBAC Group `kubeadm:cluster-admins` that has `cluster-admin` `ClusterRole` access. The User in `super-admin.conf` is now bound to the `system:masters` built-in super-powers / break-glass Group that can bypass RBAC. Before this change, the default `admin.conf` was bound to `system:masters` Group, which was undesired. Executing `kubeadm init phase kubeconfig all` or just `kubeadm init` will now generate the new `super-admin.conf` file. The cluster admin can then decide to keep the file present on a node host or move it to a safe location. `kubadm certs renew` will renew the certificate in `super-admin.conf` to one year if the file exists; if it does not exist a "MISSING" note will be printed. `kubeadm upgrade apply` for this release will migrate this particular node to the two file setup. Subsequent kubeadm releases will continue to optionally renew the certificate in `super-admin.conf` if the file exists on disk and if renew on upgrade is not disabled. `kubeadm join --control-plane` will now generate only an `admin.conf` file that has the less privileged User.
feature.author: neolit123
feature.userFacingChange: ACTION REQUIRED: kubeadm: deploy a separate "super-admin.conf" file. The User in "admin.conf" is now bound to a new RBAC Group "kubeadm:cluster-admins" that have "cluster-admin" ClusterRole access. The User in "super-admin.conf" is bound to the "system:masters" built-in super-powers / break-glass Group that can bypass RBAC. Before this change the default "admin.conf" was bound to "system:masters" Group which was undesired. Executing "kubeadm init phase kubeconfig all" or just "kubeadm init" will now generate the new "super-admin.conf" file. The cluster admin can then decide to keep the file present on a node host or move it to a safe location. "kubadm certs renew" will renew the certificate in "super-admin.conf" to one year if the file exists. If it does not exist a "MISSING" note will be printed. "kubeadm upgrade apply" for this release will migrate this particular node to the two file setup. Subsequent kubeadm releases will continue to optionally renew the certificate in "super-admin.conf" if the file exists on disk and if renew on upgrade is not disabled. "kubeadm join --control-plane" will now generate only an "admin.conf" file that has the less privileged User.

enrichment.problem: The default admin.conf generated by kubeadm was bound to the system:masters group, giving any user with that kubeconfig unrestricted, super‑user access that could bypass RBAC. This exposed highly privileged credentials on every node and was considered insecure.
enrichment.affected: Clusters initialized or joined with kubeadm that use the admin.conf kubeconfig for management. Automation, scripts, and operators that assume admin.conf provides system:masters access will need to be updated to reference super-admin.conf for break‑glass operations.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now creates a separate super-admin.conf that holds the system:masters credentials. The original admin.conf is bound to a new RBAC group kubeadm:cluster-admins, which only has the cluster-admin ClusterRole. New init, join, upgrade, and certs‑renew commands now manage these two files accordingly, allowing admins to keep or relocate the super‑admin.conf as needed.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators must adjust scripts and workflows that relied on admin.conf for full super‑user access; they should use the new super-admin.conf when break‑glass access is required. This reduces the risk of accidental privileged access from node‑local kubeconfigs and improves overall cluster security.

feature.description: Updated the generic apiserver library to produce an error if a new API server is configured with support for a data format other than JSON, YAML, or Protobuf.
feature.author: benluddy

enrichment.problem: The generic-apiserver library allowed a new API server to be configured with a data format other than the supported JSON, YAML, or Protobuf, leading to potential misconfiguration and runtime failures.
enrichment.affected: Developers/operators configuring custom or aggregated API servers that rely on the generic-apiserver library and might have attempted to enable unsupported data formats such as CBOR.
enrichment.fix: The library now validates the configured data format and returns an error at startup if an unsupported format (e.g., CBOR) is specified, preventing the API server from running with invalid serialization settings.
enrichment.impact: Prevents clusters from starting API servers with unsupported serialization formats, reducing confusing startup errors and ensuring only vetted formats are used, which improves reliability for developers of custom/aggregated API servers.

enrichment.problem: CRD validation expressions were only available behind the CustomResourceValidationExpressions feature gate, requiring users to enable the gate before they could use expressive validation in CustomResourceDefinitions.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing CustomResourceDefinitions that rely on validation expressions, as well as any workloads validated by those CRDs.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is removed and the CRD validation rule is promoted to GA, making validation expressions enabled by default and stable for all clusters.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators and developers can now use advanced validation expressions in CRDs without extra configuration, improving schema enforcement and reducing validation errors in production workloads.

feature.description:
Added new feature gate called `RuntimeClassInImageCriApi` to address `kubelet` changes needed for KEP 4216.
Noteable changes:
1. Populate new `RuntimeHandler` field in CRI's `ImageSpec` struct during image pulls from container runtimes.
2. Pass `runtimeHandler` field in `RemoveImage()` call to container runtime in `kubelet`'s image garbage collection.
feature.author: kiashok
feature.userFacingChange:
Added new feature gate called "RuntimeClassInImageCriApi" to address kubelet changes needed for KEP 4216.
Noteable changes:
1. Populate new RuntimeHandler field in CRI's ImageSpec struct during image pulls from container runtimes.
2. Pass runtimeHandler field in RemoveImage() call to container runtime in kubelet's image garbage collection

enrichment.problem: Kubelet could not convey RuntimeClass-specific runtime handler information to the container runtime during image pulls and image garbage collection, limiting support for RuntimeClass as defined in KEP-4216.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet image management and any workloads that rely on RuntimeClass (e.g., Pods specifying a RuntimeClass) were unable to correctly interact with the container runtime for image pulls and cleanup.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new feature gate `RuntimeClassInImageCriApi`. Added a `RuntimeHandler` field to the CRI `ImageSpec` struct, populated it during image pulls, and passed the field to the runtime in `RemoveImage()` calls performed by kubelet’s image garbage collector.
enrichment.impact: Enables proper RuntimeClass handling for image operations, ensuring that images are pulled and removed using the correct runtime handler. This is required for full implementation of KEP-4216 and improves compatibility with container runtimes, especially on Windows nodes.

issueContext.title: CEL: `has` macro wrongly returns false for an empty struct object
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

While migrating webhooks to CEL for one of the `oneof` structs in our CRD api, I noticed that the empty object in CEL is interpreted wrongly.

Empty map object seems to be interpreted correctly. In the example below, both map and object are sent empty (`{}`) in json output.

### What did you expect to happen?

`has(emptyObject)` returns true

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

json (captured on the client side) sent to the apiserver

```
I0829 09:13:54.107133  226332 request.go:1171] Request Body: {"apiVersion":"stas.statnett.no/v1beta2","kind":"Application","metadata":{"annotations":{"kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration":"{\"apiVersion\":\"v1beta2\",\"kind\":\"Application\",\"metadata\":{\"annotations\":{},\"name\":\"works-with-map\",\"namespace\":\"application-operator\"},\"spec\":{\"filesFrom\":[{\"mapDir\":{}},{\"emptyDir\":{}}],\"image\":\"test\",\"metadata\":{\"system\":\"stas\"}}}\n"},"name":"works-with-map","namespace":"application-operator"},"spec":{"filesFrom":[**{"mapDir":{}},{"emptyDir":{}}**],"image":"test","metadata":{"system":"stas"}}}
I0829 09:13:54.107227  226332 round_trippers.go:466] curl -v -XPOST  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "User-Agent: kubectl/4.13.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/92b1a3d" 'https://k3d-application-operator-server-0:6443/apis/stas.statnett.no/v1beta2/namespaces/application-operator/applications?fieldManager=kubectl-client-side-apply&fieldValidation=Strict'
I0829 09:13:54.129367  226332 round_trippers.go:553] POST https://k3d-application-operator-server-0:6443/apis/v1beta2/namespaces/application-operator/applications?fieldManager=kubectl-client-side-apply&fieldValidation=Strict 422 Unprocessable Entity in 22 milliseconds
I0829 09:13:54.129443  226332 round_trippers.go:570] HTTP Statistics: GetConnection 0 ms ServerProcessing 21 ms Duration 22 ms
I0829 09:13:54.129453  226332 round_trippers.go:577] Response Headers:
I

enrichment.problem: The CEL `has` macro incorrectly returned false for empty struct objects when a CRD's openAPIV3Schema lacked both `properties` and `additionalProperties`. This caused validation to reject objects that should be considered present, breaking webhook and other CEL-based validation for CRDs with empty structs.
enrichment.affected: Operators and developers who define CRDs that include empty struct fields and use CEL validation expressions (such as admission webhooks).
enrichment.fix: CEL handling in the API server was updated to correctly interpret schemas without `properties` or `additionalProperties`. The `has` macro now returns true for empty struct objects, aligning CEL behavior with expected semantics.
enrichment.impact: Users leveraging CEL expressions for CRD validation (e.g., admission webhooks) can now rely on accurate `has` checks for empty structs, preventing false validation failures and enabling correct policy enforcement.

feature.description: Added `apiextensions_apiserver_update_ratcheting_time` metric for tracking time taken during requests by feature `CRDValidationRatcheting`.
feature.author: alexzielenski
feature.userFacingChange: Adds `apiextensions_apiserver_update_ratcheting_time` metric for tracking time taken during requests by feature `CRDValidationRatcheting`

enrichment.problem: There was no metric to measure the time spent processing requests related to the CRDValidationRatcheting feature in the API extensions server, making it difficult for operators to observe and diagnose performance impacts of CRD validation ratcheting.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CustomResourceDefinitions that rely on CRD validation ratcheting; cluster admins and developers monitoring apiserver performance.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `apiextensions_apiserver_update_ratcheting_time` metric, which records the latency of requests processed by the CRDValidationRatcheting feature in the API extensions apiserver.
enrichment.impact: Provides visibility into the performance of CRD validation ratcheting, enabling operators to monitor latency, set alerts, and tune the feature if needed, improving cluster observability and troubleshooting.

feature.description: Promoted `PodHostIPs` condition to `beta`.
feature.author: wzshiming
feature.userFacingChange: Promote PodHostIPs condition to beta.

enrichment.problem: Previously there was no standard condition on a Pod indicating the assigned host IP addresses, making it difficult for users and controllers to reliably observe when a Pod had a host IP and to react to changes.
enrichment.affected: All workloads that need to know a Pod's host IPs, such as network plugins, custom controllers, and monitoring systems, as well as users querying Pod status.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `PodHostIPs` condition on the Pod status and promotes it to beta. The condition is set by the kubelet when host IPs are allocated and is exposed via the API server.
enrichment.impact: Users, controllers, and monitoring tools can now watch a concrete condition to know when a Pod has host IPs, improving reliability of network‑related automation and observability. As a beta feature it is stable enough for production use while still allowing feedback before GA.

feature.description: Added `job_pods_creation_total` metrics for tracking Pods created by the Job controller labeled by events which triggered the Pod creation.
feature.author: dejanzele
feature.userFacingChange: Add job_pods_creation_total metrics for tracking Pods created by the Job controller labeled by events which triggered the Pod creation

enrichment.problem: Cluster operators and users had no built-in way to observe how many Pods the Job controller creates and which events (e.g., completions, backoffs, parallelism changes) triggered each creation, limiting troubleshooting and capacity planning.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch workloads with Job objects and any monitoring systems that scrape controller‑manager metrics. Cluster operators gain more insight into Job controller behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new Prometheus metric `job_pods_creation_total` that the Job controller increments each time it creates a Pod. The metric is labeled with the specific event that caused the creation, giving granular visibility into Job‑related pod lifecycle activity.
enrichment.impact: Provides concrete observability for Job workloads, enabling better alerting, debugging, and capacity planning. Operators can now monitor pod‑creation patterns per Job and correlate them with trigger events, improving reliability and performance tuning.

feature.description: The KMSv2 features with feature gates `KMSv2` and `KMSv2KDF` are promoted to `GA`.  The `KMSv1` feature gate is now disabled by default.
feature.author: ritazh
feature.userFacingChange: The KMSv2 feature with feature gates `KMSv2` and `KMSv2KDF` are promoted to GA.  The `KMSv1` feature gate is now disabled by default.

issueContext.title: [KMSv2] update code to mark API as GA in v1.29
issueContext.body:
I think all of the changes will be focused around allowing `v2` as an acceptable value in addition to `v2beta1` (with associated unit/integration tests):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76b06ee239a893dece6eae861090f06df994a878/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/value/encrypt/envelope/kmsv2/envelope.go#L55-L56

/sig auth
/triage accepted
/assign ritazh
/milestone v1.29

enrichment.problem: KMS v1 was the default encryption provider and lacked the improvements of KMS v2 (e.g., better key derivation). Users had to manually enable the newer, more secure KMS v2 functionality, and the default KMS v1 could lead to less secure configurations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using envelope encryption for Secrets with KMS providers, especially those that had KMS v1 enabled by default.
enrichment.fix: Promote the KMS v2 feature gates (`KMSv2` and `KMSv2KDF`) to GA, making them enabled by default. Disable the `KMSv1` feature gate by default, requiring explicit opt‑in for the older implementation.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on secret encryption automatically get the more secure and stable KMS v2 implementation without extra configuration, improving overall data‑at‑rest security. Administrators using KMS v1 must now explicitly enable its feature gate, ensuring they are aware of the legacy behavior.

feature.description: Promoted `PodReplacementPolicy` to `beta`.
feature.author: dejanzele
feature.userFacingChange: Promote PodReplacementPolicy to beta.

enrichment.problem: PodReplacementPolicy was only available as an alpha feature, requiring a feature gate and lacking stability guarantees, which prevented its reliable use in production workloads.
enrichment.affected: Users and administrators of workloads that rely on controlled pod replacement (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets) and developers in the Apps SIG seeking a stable API.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to beta, making the PodReplacementPolicy field stable, default-enabled, and no longer gated, so clusters can configure pod replacement behavior without using alpha APIs.
enrichment.impact: Enables broader adoption of deterministic pod replacement during node maintenance or upgrades, improving workload reliability and reducing operational friction for users of Deployments, StatefulSets, and other controllers.

feature.description: `etcd`: image is now based on `v3.5.9`.
feature.author: mzaian
feature.userFacingChange: etcd: build image for v3.5.10

enrichment.problem: The etcd container image used by Kubernetes was based on an older version (v3.5.9) and needed to be updated to include the latest upstream fixes and improvements.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the built‑in etcd component; primarily control‑plane nodes that host etcd.
enrichment.fix: The etcd image is rebuilt and now based on version v3.5.10, bringing in the upstream changes from that release.
enrichment.impact: Control‑plane components that rely on etcd will run on a newer, more stable version with bug fixes and security patches, reducing the risk of known etcd issues affecting clusters.

feature.description: Bumped `cel-go` to `v0.17.7` and introduced set `ext` library with new options.
feature.author: cici37
feature.userFacingChange: Bump cel-go to v0.17.7 and introduce set ext library with new options.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes components were using an older version of the CEL library (cel-go) which lacked recent bug fixes, security patches, and did not provide the new set extension library with additional options needed for advanced expression handling in API validation and admission.
enrichment.affected: Components that evaluate CEL expressions (primarily kube-apiserver and any controllers/admission plugins that rely on CEL) will see updated behavior and new capabilities.
enrichment.fix: The CEL dependency is upgraded to cel-go v0.17.7 and the new `set` extension library is introduced, exposing additional configuration options for expression evaluation.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability and security of CEL‑based features such as CRD validation, admission control, and other expression‑driven logic. Users can now leverage the new set extension options without needing external patches.

feature.description: The `SidecarContainers` feature has graduated to `beta` and is enabled by default.
feature.author: gjkim42
feature.userFacingChange: The SidecarContainers feature has graduated to beta and is enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: Not applicable – the change is a feature graduation rather than a bug fix.
enrichment.affected: Pods that declare sidecarContainers, and any controllers that create such pods (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets). The kube-apiserver and kubelet are updated to recognize and enforce the new field.
enrichment.fix: The SidecarContainers feature gate has been graduated to beta and is now enabled by default, making the sidecarContainers field in pod specs available without requiring explicit enabling.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use the sidecarContainers field out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying sidecar lifecycle management and enabling more robust sidecar handling in production workloads.

feature.description: `cluster/gce`: added webhook to replace `PersistentVolumeLabel` admission controller.
feature.author: andrewsykim
feature.userFacingChange: cluster/gce: add webhook to replace PersistentVolumeLabel admission controller

enrichment.problem: The built‑in PersistentVolumeLabel admission controller is being removed, which would stop automatic labeling of PersistentVolumes in GCE clusters and could break workloads that rely on those topology labels.
enrichment.affected: Clusters on the GCE cloud provider that create PersistentVolumes and rely on automatic topology labeling.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a mutating admission webhook for GCE that replicates the behavior of the old PersistentVolumeLabel admission controller, automatically adding the appropriate GCE‑specific labels to newly created PersistentVolumes.
enrichment.impact: GCE clusters retain the same PV labeling semantics after the admission controller is removed, preventing disruption of scheduling and volume binding that depend on zone/region labels.

feature.description: Priority and Fairness feature is now `stable`, the feature gate will be removed in `v1.31`.
feature.author: tkashem
feature.userFacingChange: - Priority and Fairness feature is stable in 1.29, the feature gate will be removed in 1.31

enrichment.problem: The Priority and Fairness feature was in beta and required a feature gate to be enabled, adding configuration overhead and uncertainty about its future stability.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and any workloads that rely on API server request prioritization and fairness.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to stable in v1.29 and the corresponding feature gate will be removed in v1.31, making it always enabled without extra configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to enable or manage a feature gate for request prioritization and fairness, simplifying API server configuration and providing GA guarantees for workloads that depend on predictable request handling.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go `1.21.4`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.21.4

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, missing recent language bug fixes and security updates.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go toolchain.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.21.4.
enrichment.impact: Users receive binaries that benefit from Go 1.21.4's security patches, performance improvements, and bug fixes, while maintaining API compatibility. No functional changes are introduced.

feature.description:
A customizable `OrderedScoreFuncs()` function was introduced. Out-of-tree plugins 
that used the scheduler's preemption interface could implement this function
for custom preemption preferences or return nil to keep the current behavior.
feature.author: lianghao208
feature.userFacingChange: A customizable OrderedScoreFuncs() function is introduced. Out-of-tree plugins that use scheduler's preemption interface can implement this function for custom preemption preferences, or return nil to keep current behavior.

enrichment.problem: Out‑of‑tree scheduler plugins that used the preemption interface could not control the order in which scoring functions were applied, forcing them to use the built‑in preemption logic.
enrichment.affected: Out‑of‑tree scheduler plugins that implement the preemption interface; any workloads that rely on custom preemption behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a customizable OrderedScoreFuncs() hook. Plugins can implement this function to supply their own ordered list of scoring functions for preemption, or return nil to retain the existing default behavior.
enrichment.impact: Plugins can now express custom preemption preferences, enabling more precise pod eviction decisions and better workload placement. This gives cluster operators finer‑grained control over resource utilization without breaking existing plugins.

feature.description: Bumped distroless-iptables to 0.4.1 based on Go `1.21.3`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Bump distroless-iptables to 0.4.1 based on Go 1.21.3

enrichment.problem: The previous distroless-iptables image was built with an older Go version and may include outdated iptables binaries or missing security fixes.
enrichment.affected: Projects and CI pipelines that use the distroless-iptables image, especially SIG Testing infrastructure.
enrichment.fix: Bump the distroless-iptables image to version 0.4.1, which is compiled with Go 1.21.3.
enrichment.impact: Test environments and any workloads that depend on the distroless-iptables image receive up‑to‑date binaries and security patches, reducing the risk of subtle networking issues in CI and testing.

deprecation.description: Stopped accepting component configuration for `kube-proxy` and `kubelet` during `kubeadm upgrade plan --config`. This was a legacy behavior that was not well supported for upgrades and could be used only at the plan stage to determine if the configuration for these components stored in the cluster needs manual version migration. In the future, `kubeadm` will attempt alternative component config migration approaches.
deprecation.author: chendave
deprecation.userFacingChange: ACTION REQUIRED: stop accepting component configuration for kube-proxy and kubelet during `kubeadm upgrade plan --config`. This is a legacy behavior that is not well supported for upgrades and can be used only at the plan stage to determine if the configuration for these components stored in the cluster needs manual version  migration. In the future, kubeadm will attempt alternative component config migration approaches.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm upgrade plan --config incorrectly accepted component configuration for kube-proxy and kubelet, a legacy behavior that was not fully supported for upgrades and could only be used to check if manual version migration was needed.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators running `kubeadm upgrade plan --config` with kube-proxy or kubelet component configuration.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm no longer accepts component configuration for kube-proxy and kubelet during the upgrade plan phase. Future kubeadm versions will use alternative migration methods for these component configs.
enrichment.impact: Users who include kube-proxy or kubelet component configs in their kubeadm upgrade plan files will see the command fail and must remove those sections or rely on the new migration approach. This prevents unsupported upgrade paths and reduces risk of broken clusters during upgrades.

apiChange.description: Fixes accidental enablement of the new alpha `optionalOldSelf` API field in CustomResourceDefinition validation rules, which should only be allowed to be set when the CRDValidationRatcheting feature gate is enabled. Existing CustomResourceDefinition objects which have the field set will retain it on update, but new CustomResourceDefinition objects will not be permitted to set the field while the CRDValidationRatcheting feature gate is disabled.
apiChange.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: The new alpha `optionalOldSelf` field in CRD validation rules could be set even when the CRDValidationRatcheting feature gate was disabled, allowing unintended use of an unfinished API feature.
enrichment.affected: Users creating new CustomResourceDefinition objects with the `optionalOldSelf` field while the CRDValidationRatcheting gate is disabled, and any existing CRDs that already contain the field.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now enforces that `optionalOldSelf` can only be specified when the CRDValidationRatcheting feature gate is enabled. Existing CRDs that already have the field keep it on update, but new CRDs cannot set it while the gate is off.
enrichment.impact: Prevents clusters from unintentionally using an alpha validation field, ensuring validation behavior matches the intended feature‑gate state and avoiding potential mis‑configurations.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.21.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, missing recent language improvements, bug fixes, and security patches.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries and any workloads that depend on the binaries are indirectly affected; the change is transparent to end‑users.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.21.6.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) benefit from Go 1.21.6's runtime improvements, security fixes, and performance enhancements. No functional change for users, but provides a more secure and efficient foundation.

bugOrRegression.description: Allow deletion of pods that use raw block volumes on node reboot
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Pods that used raw block volumes could not be deleted when a node rebooted, leaving them stuck in a terminating state.
enrichment.affected: Workloads using raw block volumes on nodes that undergo a reboot were unable to terminate, potentially causing resource leaks and deployment issues.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet’s pod termination logic was updated to allow deletion of pods that have raw block volume mounts during a node reboot, ensuring proper cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Users running workloads with raw block volumes will no longer encounter stuck pods after node reboots, improving reliability and freeing node resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix an issue where kubectl apply could panic when imported as a library
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: kubectl apply could panic (crash) when the kubectl package is imported and used as a library, causing programs that embed it to abort.
enrichment.affected: Programs that import the kubectl library (e.g., custom controllers, CI/CD tools) could experience a panic and termination.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks and error handling in the apply implementation to prevent the panic condition, ensuring the library returns an error instead of crashing.
enrichment.impact: Prevents crashes for applications that embed kubectl's apply functionality, improving stability and reliability of automation tools and custom controllers that rely on the library.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: Mount point may become local without calling NodePublishVolume after node rebooting.
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: After a node reboot, a CSI volume mount point could be treated as a local mount without the kubelet invoking NodePublishVolume, leading to incorrect volume state and potential data access issues.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes nodes running CSI-backed PersistentVolumes; pods that rely on those volumes may have experienced mount failures or data access problems after node reboots.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now ensures that NodePublishVolume is called for CSI volumes after a node reboot, correctly re-establishing the mount and preventing the mount point from being misidentified as local.
enrichment.impact: Prevents volume mount inconsistencies and possible data unavailability for workloads using CSI persistent volumes after node restarts, improving reliability of storage operations.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression since 1.24 in the scheduling framework when overriding MultiPoint plugins (e.g. default plugins).
  The incorrect loop logic might lead to a plugin being loaded multiple times, consequently preventing any Pod from being scheduled, which is unexpected.
bugOrRegression.author: caohe

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in v1.24 caused the scheduling framework to load MultiPoint plugins (including overridden default plugins) multiple times due to incorrect loop logic, resulting in no Pods being scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Users who override MultiPoint scheduler plugins (including default plugins) in clusters running Kubernetes 1.24 and later.
enrichment.fix: The loop logic in the scheduling framework was corrected so that MultiPoint plugins are loaded only once, restoring proper plugin handling and allowing Pods to be scheduled normally.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that override MultiPoint scheduler plugins could become unable to schedule any Pods, leading to service disruption. The fix restores normal pod scheduling functionality.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed migration of in-tree vSphere volumes to the CSI driver.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: In-tree vSphere volume migration to the CSI driver could fail, preventing clusters from moving to the supported CSI implementation.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that had vSphere in-tree persistent volumes and attempted to migrate them to the vSphere CSI driver.
enrichment.fix: Corrected the migration logic so that vSphere in-tree volumes are properly detected and transitioned to the vSphere CSI driver during upgrade or migration operations.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using vSphere in-tree volumes can now safely migrate to the CSI driver without storage disruption, ensuring continuity and compliance with the deprecated in-tree plugin removal.

bugOrRegression.description: QueueingHint implementation for NodeAffinity is reverted because we found potential scenarios where events that make Pods schedulable could be missed.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The new QueueingHint implementation for NodeAffinity could miss events that make Pods schedulable, causing Pods with NodeAffinity to remain unscheduled.
enrichment.affected: Any Pods that specify NodeAffinity could have been unschedulable due to missed events.
enrichment.fix: Revert the QueueingHint changes for NodeAffinity, restoring the previous scheduling logic so that all relevant events are processed.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable pod scheduling for workloads that use NodeAffinity, preventing delays or failures in pod placement.

bugOrRegression.description: QueueingHint implementation for NodeUnschedulable is reverted because we found potential scenarios where events that make Pods schedulable could be missed.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The newly added QueueingHint for the NodeUnschedulable condition could miss events that make previously unschedulable Pods become schedulable, causing those Pods to remain pending.
enrichment.affected: Pods that rely on the scheduler to notice node unschedulable/schedulable transitions could remain unscheduled.
enrichment.fix: The QueueingHint implementation for NodeUnschedulable is reverted, restoring the previous behavior so that all relevant events are processed correctly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that Pods are correctly re‑evaluated for scheduling when node conditions change, preventing silent scheduling failures and improving overall scheduler reliability.

other.description: Reverts the EventedPLEG feature (beta, but disabled by default) back to alpha for a known issue
other.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: The EventedPLEG feature, promoted to beta (though disabled by default), introduced a known issue that could cause incorrect pod lifecycle event handling when the feature is enabled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enabled the EventedPLEG beta feature, primarily affecting the kubelet's pod lifecycle handling on nodes.
enrichment.fix: Reverted EventedPLEG back to its previous alpha stage, removing the buggy beta implementation and restoring the stable alpha behavior.
enrichment.impact: Users who had enabled the EventedPLEG beta no longer encounter the issue; however, they lose any beta‑level improvements until the problem is resolved and the feature can be safely re‑promoted.

feature.description: Add process_start_time_seconds to /metrics/slis endpoint of all components
feature.author: richabanker

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes components did not expose a metric for the process start time, limiting the ability to track component uptime and compute Service Level Indicators (SLIs).
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, etc.) now expose the new metric.
enrichment.fix: Added a new metric `process_start_time_seconds` to the `/metrics/slis` endpoint for all core components, exposing the Unix timestamp of when each process started.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor component start times directly via Prometheus, enabling better uptime tracking, alerting, and SLI computation for reliability monitoring.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.7

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, missing recent Go runtime bug fixes, performance improvements, and security updates.
enrichment.affected: Users who build Kubernetes from source or rely on official binaries; downstream vendors packaging Kubernetes.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile the codebase with Go 1.21.7, incorporating the latest Go toolchain changes.
enrichment.impact: Developers and downstream distributors building Kubernetes from source get binaries that include Go runtime security patches and performance enhancements, reducing potential vulnerabilities and improving overall stability.

feature.description: update setcap/debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.1

enrichment.problem: The setcap binary and Debian base image used in Kubernetes build processes were outdated, potentially missing security updates and bug fixes.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI systems that build Kubernetes components using the setcap/debian-base image.
enrichment.fix: The Dockerfile/CI images have been updated to use the Debian bookworm-v1.0.1 base and the accompanying setcap package version.
enrichment.impact: Build environments and CI pipelines now use a fresher, supported OS base, reducing exposure to known OS vulnerabilities and improving compatibility with newer tooling.

feature.description: update distroless-iptables to v0.4.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The previous distroless-iptables image (v0.4.4) contained known bugs and security vulnerabilities in its iptables implementation, which could cause incorrect firewall rules or be exploitable in clusters.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy (or other components that rely on the distroless-iptables image) were affected; the update resolves the issue for those workloads.
enrichment.fix: The distroless-iptables dependency was updated to version v0.4.5, which includes upstream bug fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Kubernetes networking components that embed the distroless-iptables image, such as kube-proxy, now operate with more reliable and secure iptables handling, reducing the risk of networking failures or security exposures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix deprecated version for pod_scheduling_duration_seconds that caused the metric to be hidden by default in 1.29.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: The pod_scheduling_duration_seconds metric was registered with a deprecated version, causing it to be hidden by default in Kubernetes 1.29, so users could not see scheduling latency data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.29 that depend on the pod_scheduling_duration_seconds metric for monitoring or alerting.
enrichment.fix: Updated the metric registration to use the current, non‑deprecated version, restoring the pod_scheduling_duration_seconds metric to be enabled and exported by default.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting systems that rely on pod scheduling latency can now collect the metric again, improving observability of scheduler performance.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that caused policies which were using CRD parameters to fail to synchronize
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects that referenced CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) parameters failed to synchronize, causing the policies not to be applied.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CRD parameters; administrators defining such policies.
enrichment.fix: The bug in the admission control implementation was corrected so that policies using CRD parameters now synchronize correctly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that admission policies relying on CRD parameters are enforced, restoring expected validation behavior and preventing unintended workloads from being admitted.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.29 regression in "kubeadm init" that caused a user-specified --kubeconfig file to be ignored.
bugOrRegression.author: avorima

enrichment.problem: `kubeadm init` ignored a user‑provided `--kubeconfig` flag, causing the initialization process to fall back to the default kubeconfig and disregarding the intended configuration.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm init` with a custom `--kubeconfig` file, typically during initial cluster bootstrap.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed so that `kubeadm init` now correctly respects the `--kubeconfig` argument, using the specified file for cluster bootstrap.
enrichment.impact: Operators can reliably supply a custom kubeconfig during cluster initialization, avoiding unexpected configuration defaults and reducing the risk of mis‑configured clusters.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy in 1.27 and later
  that could result in some updates getting lost (e.g., when a service gets a
  new endpoint, the rules for the new endpoint might not be added until
  much later).
bugOrRegression.author: hakman

enrichment.problem: A race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy could cause updates to be lost, such as when a Service gains a new endpoint the corresponding iptables rules might not be added promptly.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy in iptables mode (Kubernetes 1.27+). Services that add or remove endpoints could experience delayed or missing routing rules.
enrichment.fix: The race condition in kube-proxy’s iptables code path is corrected so that endpoint updates are applied reliably without being delayed or dropped.
enrichment.impact: Service traffic routing remains accurate and up‑to‑date, preventing stale or missing endpoint rules that could lead to connectivity issues for workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: If a pvc has an empty storageClassName, persistentvolume controller won't try to assign a default StorageClass
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When a PersistentVolumeClaim had an empty storageClassName, the persistentvolume controller treated it as specified and did not fall back to the cluster's default StorageClass, leaving the PVC unbound.
enrichment.affected: Users creating PVCs without a storageClassName (or with an empty string), affecting workloads that rely on those PVCs such as Deployments, StatefulSets, and Jobs.
enrichment.fix: The persistentvolume controller now treats an empty storageClassName as unspecified and will attempt to assign the default StorageClass during PVC provisioning.
enrichment.impact: PVCs that omitted a storage class (or set it to an empty string) will now bind automatically, preventing pod startup failures and reducing the need for manual PVC edits.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: do not upload kubelet patch configuration into `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu
