enrichment.problem: kubeadm was uploading the kubelet patch configuration into the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap, overwriting any existing custom kubelet configuration stored there.
enrichment.affected: Clusters set up with kubeadm where the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap is used to hold custom kubelet configuration.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm code path was changed to stop uploading the kubelet patch configuration into the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap, preserving user‑provided kubelet settings.
enrichment.impact: Users who rely on custom kubelet configuration in the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap will no longer see their settings unintentionally overwritten during kubeadm init/join, preventing unexpected kubelet behavior on nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the --rootfs global flag does not work with "kubeadm upgrade node" for control plane nodes.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: The --rootfs global flag was ignored when running `kubeadm upgrade node` on control‑plane nodes, preventing upgrades that rely on a custom root filesystem.
enrichment.affected: Administrators upgrading control‑plane nodes with `kubeadm upgrade node` and specifying a custom rootfs were unable to complete the upgrade.
enrichment.fix: Updated kubeadm to correctly honor the --rootfs flag during `upgrade node` operations for control‑plane nodes, ensuring the specified root filesystem is used.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now reliably upgrade control‑plane nodes that use a non‑default rootfs (e.g., in container‑based or chroot environments) without upgrade failures.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.8

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version that no longer receives security patches and may lack recent performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries and the clusters that run them may benefit from the updated Go toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.21.8, incorporating the latest compiler fixes, security patches, and language/runtime enhancements.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, etc.) are now built on a more secure and performant Go runtime, reducing the risk of Go‑related vulnerabilities and improving overall binary performance and compatibility.

feature.description: update distroless-iptables to v0.4.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes distribution was using an older version of the distroless-iptables image, which could contain bugs or missing fixes.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kube-proxy or any workloads that depend on the distroless-iptables image.
enrichment.fix: Update the distroless-iptables image reference to version v0.4.6, pulling in upstream bug fixes and improvements.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using components that rely on the distroless-iptables image (e.g., kube-proxy) will run with the latest iptables binaries, reducing the chance of networking issues and potential security exposures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix error when trying to expand a volume that does not require node expansion
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Expanding a PersistentVolume that does not require node expansion resulted in an error, preventing the expansion from succeeding.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where users attempt to expand PVCs backed by CSI drivers that handle expansion without node‑level intervention.
enrichment.fix: Added logic to detect when a volume does not need node expansion and skip the node‑expansion step, avoiding the spurious error.
enrichment.impact: Users can successfully expand PVCs even when the underlying volume driver does not require node‑level changes, improving reliability of storage operations.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that an init container with containerRestartPolicy with `Always` cannot update its state from terminated to non-terminated for the pod with restartPolicy with `Never` or `OnFailure`.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: When a pod's restartPolicy is set to Never or OnFailure, an init container that has containerRestartPolicy set to Always could not transition its state from terminated back to non‑terminated, causing the init container (and possibly the pod) to be stuck in a terminated state.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use an init container with containerRestartPolicy=Always together with a pod restartPolicy of Never or OnFailure. Users deploying such workloads experienced stale pod status.
enrichment.fix: The bug in the pod lifecycle handling was fixed so that init containers with containerRestartPolicy=Always can correctly update their state from terminated to running even when the pod's restartPolicy is Never or OnFailure.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers to keep running under a Never or OnFailure pod restartPolicy now behave correctly, preventing pods from being stuck and improving reliability for workloads that use this combination of policies.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed cleanup of Pod volume mounts when a file was used as a subpath.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When a file (rather than a directory) was used as a subPath in a pod's volume mount, kubelet failed to properly clean up the mount point after the pod was terminated, leaving stale mounts on the node.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use a file as a subPath in a volume mount on nodes, potentially leading to leaked mounts after pod deletion.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now correctly removes the volume mount for file‑based subPath volumes during pod teardown, ensuring all associated mount points are cleaned up.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accumulation of orphaned mounts that could exhaust node resources or cause mount‑related errors on subsequent pod starts, improving node stability and reliability for workloads that use file subPath volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed the disruption controller's PDB status synchronization to maintain all PDB conditions during an update.
bugOrRegression.author: dhenkel92

enrichment.problem: The disruption controller failed to retain all PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) conditions when synchronizing status during an update, causing conditions to be dropped and potentially giving users inaccurate PDB status.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using PodDisruptionBudgets could see inaccurate PDB conditions during controller updates, affecting workloads that depend on PDB for high‑availability eviction logic.
enrichment.fix: The controller now preserves every existing PDB condition when updating the PDB status, ensuring no condition is lost during synchronization.
enrichment.impact: Users relying on PDBs for safe pod evictions will see correct, complete status information, preventing unintended pod disruptions and improving cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue calculating total CPU usage reported for Windows nodes
bugOrRegression.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: The kubelet incorrectly calculated the total CPU usage reported for Windows nodes, leading to inaccurate CPU usage metrics.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with Windows nodes; any tooling or components that consume the node's CPU usage metrics (e.g., metrics-server, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler).
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the CPU usage calculation logic in the kubelet for Windows nodes to correctly sum CPU usage across all pods and system components.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate CPU usage data for Windows nodes, ensuring reliable monitoring, autoscaling decisions, and capacity planning for workloads running on Windows.

bugOrRegression.description: Prevent watch cache starvation by moving its watch to separate RPC and add a SeparateCacheWatchRPC feature flag to disable this behavior
bugOrRegression.author: mengqiy

enrichment.problem: A high volume of watch requests could starve the watch cache in the API server, leading to delayed or missed watch events for clients.
enrichment.affected: Clients that depend on the watch API (e.g., controllers, operators, custom tools) could experience delayed or missed events under heavy watch load.
enrichment.fix: The watch cache is moved to a separate RPC channel, isolating it from other watch traffic. A new feature gate, SeparateCacheWatchRPC, can be used to toggle this behavior.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability and latency of watch streams for all clients, preventing cache starvation especially in clusters with many watch consumers.

bugOrRegression.description: Restore --verify-only function in code generation wrappers.
bugOrRegression.author: skitt

enrichment.problem: The `--verify-only` flag in the code generation wrappers was removed or non‑functional, preventing users from verifying generated code without modifying files.
enrichment.affected: Users of Kubernetes API machinery code generators (e.g., deepcopy-gen, defaulter-gen) and CI systems that rely on `--verify-only` for validation.
enrichment.fix: Re‑implemented and restored the `--verify-only` functionality in the code generation wrappers, enabling dry‑run verification again.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines can now safely verify that generated code is up‑to‑date without altering source files, improving reliability of code‑gen workflows and preventing accidental code drift.

bugOrRegression.description: Updates google.golang.org/protobuf to v1.33.0 to resolve CVE-2024-24786
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: A vulnerable version of the google.golang.org/protobuf library (pre‑v1.33.0) was used in Kubernetes, exposing the system to CVE‑2024‑24786.
enrichment.affected: All components that serialize/deserialize protobuf objects, such as the API server, kubelet, controller‑manager, scheduler, kubectl, and other control‑plane and client binaries.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components were rebuilt to depend on protobuf v1.33.0, which contains the patches that remediate CVE‑2024‑24786.
enrichment.impact: The security flaw is mitigated, preventing potential attacks that could compromise the control plane or workloads. Clusters updated with this release are no longer vulnerable.

other.description: Etcd: Update to version 3.5.12
other.author: bzsuni

enrichment.problem: The cluster's etcd version (3.5.11) contained known bugs and security vulnerabilities that could affect data integrity and stability of the control‑plane state store.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that run the default etcd instance; any control‑plane component (kube‑apiserver, controller‑manager, scheduler, kubelet) that reads/writes cluster state via etcd.
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the bundled etcd component to version 3.5.12, which includes upstream bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes clusters using the built‑in etcd gain a more reliable and secure data store, reducing risk of data loss or control‑plane disruption.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using containers, init containers, and ephemeral containers with the envFrom field populated.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.9

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries built from source (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are now built with Go 1.21.9.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes binaries are now compiled with Go 1.21.9, updating the language toolchain used for building the project.
enrichment.impact: Provides security fixes, performance improvements, and bug fixes from the newer Go release to all Kubernetes components, and ensures continued support with an up‑to‑date compiler.

feature.description: update debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.2
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Debian base image used for building Kubernetes binaries was outdated, potentially lacking recent security fixes and package updates.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from the Debian base (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy) and any downstream images that rely on this base.
enrichment.fix: Updated the debian-base to the newer bookworm-v1.0.2 release, bringing in the latest OS packages and security patches for all components built from this base.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that newly built Kubernetes binaries include up‑to‑date OS components, reducing the risk of known vulnerabilities and improving overall stability of the release.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix pod restart after node reboot when NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate is enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled
bugOrRegression.author: bertinatto

enrichment.problem: Pods did not restart automatically after a node reboot when the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate was enabled and the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature gate was disabled.
enrichment.affected: Nodes with NewVolumeManagerReconstruction enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled; pods that rely on read-write-once volume semantics on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic that determines pod restart after node reboot has been corrected to handle the combination of NewVolumeManagerReconstruction being on and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod being off, ensuring pods are recreated as expected.
enrichment.impact: Workloads on nodes using the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature (with SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled) will now recover correctly after a node reboot, avoiding unintended pod downtime and service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Golang.org/x/net is bumped to v0.23.0 to address CVE-2023-45288
bugOrRegression.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: The Go net library (golang.org/x/net) used by Kubernetes components contained CVE-2023-45288, a security vulnerability that could be exploited to affect cluster operations.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries that depend on golang.org/x/net (e.g., kube-apiserver, kubelet, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kube-proxy, kubectl) were vulnerable.
enrichment.fix: The dependency is upgraded to golang.org/x/net v0.23.0, which includes the patch that resolves CVE-2023-45288.
enrichment.impact: Mitigates the security risk across all affected Kubernetes components, preventing potential attacks that could compromise cluster stability or data.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression in watch stability by serving watch requests without a resourceVersion from the watch cache by default, as in <1.27 (disabling the change in #115096 by default). This mitigates the impact of an etcd watch bug (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/17555). If the 1.27 change in #115096 to serve these requests from underlying storage is still desired despite the impact on watch stability, it can be re-enabled with a `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: Kube-apiserver regression introduced in v1.27 caused watch requests to be served from underlying storage without a resourceVersion, leading to unstable watch streams due to an etcd watch bug.
enrichment.affected: Any component that consumes watch streams (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom operators) experienced intermittent watch failures.
enrichment.fix: Restores pre‑1.27 behavior: watch requests are served from the watch cache without a resourceVersion by default. The 1.27 change can be re‑enabled via the WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Restores stable watch behavior for controllers, operators, kubectl and other clients that rely on watch streams, mitigating failures caused by the etcd watch bug.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic in the command "kubeadm certs check-expiration" when "/etc/kubernetes/pki" exists but cannot be read.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The command `kubeadm certs check-expiration` panics and crashes when the PKI directory `/etc/kubernetes/pki` exists but the process lacks read permissions, preventing administrators from checking certificate expiry.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using kubeadm to verify certificate expiration on clusters where the PKI directory exists but is not readable (e.g., due to permission issues).
enrichment.fix: Added proper error handling to detect unreadable PKI directory and report a user-friendly error instead of panicking, allowing the command to complete gracefully.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can safely run the certificate expiration check even on mis‑configured or permission‑restricted nodes, avoiding unexpected tool crashes and enabling proactive certificate renewal.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

bugOrRegression.description: OpenAPI V2 will no longer publish aggregated apiserver OpenAPI for group-versions not matching the APIService specified group version
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: OpenAPI v2 of aggregated API servers incorrectly published schemas for group-versions that did not match the APIService's declared group version, leading to misleading API discovery information for clients.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that retrieve OpenAPI v2 specs from aggregated API servers could see incorrect definitions. The change affects the API discovery flow for those APIs.
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI v2 generation logic now filters out group-versions that do not align with the APIService's specified group version, ensuring only matching group-versions are published.
enrichment.impact: Clients (e.g., kubectl, IDEs, code generators) receive accurate OpenAPI specifications, preventing confusion and potential errors when consuming aggregated APIs. Minimal impact on existing workflows; only mismatched schemas are removed.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that a pod may remain unscheduled if any PreFilter plugin returns nodes that do not exist.
bugOrRegression.author: chengjoey

enrichment.problem: When a PreFilter plugin returned a list of nodes that do not exist in the cluster, the scheduler could not find a suitable node and left the pod in a pending state indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using custom or built‑in PreFilter plugins that might return nonexistent nodes; pods could remain unscheduled.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now verifies that nodes returned by any PreFilter plugin actually exist before proceeding, preventing pods from getting stuck unscheduled.
enrichment.impact: Pods are no longer left pending due to invalid node lists, improving cluster reliability and reducing manual intervention for affected workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.29.0 regression that introduced a possible data race that could cause panics in kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes v1.29.0 created a data race in the kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler code paths, which could trigger panics and crash these control‑plane components.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded to v1.29.0 that run the kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler could experience panics and loss of control‑plane functionality.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected by adding proper synchronization (removing the data race) in the affected code paths, preventing the panics in both kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unexpected crashes of the controller manager and scheduler, ensuring the control plane remains stable and avoiding cluster‑wide outages for workloads that rely on scheduling and controller functions.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug when using external CA mode and trying to upgrade to 1.29 using "kubeadm upgrade apply". Show a warning that kubeadm cannot sign the new "super-admin.conf" as the host does not have a CA and show some instructions on how to manually migrate to the separate "admin.conf" and "super-admin.conf" kubeconfig files.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When clusters are configured to use an external Certificate Authority, running `kubeadm upgrade apply` to upgrade to v1.29 fails to sign the new `super-admin.conf` because the host does not possess a CA, leading to missing or invalid admin kubeconfig.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use kubeadm with an external CA and are upgraded to Kubernetes 1.29.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now detects the external‑CA scenario during upgrade, emits a clear warning that it cannot sign `super-admin.conf`, and provides step‑by‑step instructions for manually migrating to the separate `admin.conf` and `super-admin.conf` kubeconfig files.
enrichment.impact: Prevents upgrade failures for clusters using external CAs and gives operators a reliable manual migration path, improving upgrade reliability and reducing downtime.

other.description: For apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, we are renaming the label for etcd to be "storage_cluster_id" instead of "cluster" to to reduce conflict and be very specific.
other.author: dims

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric used the generic label name "cluster" for the etcd storage cluster, which could conflict with other metrics and was not specific enough.
enrichment.affected: Users of the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric (e.g., Prometheus queries, dashboards) and any tooling that relies on the old "cluster" label.
enrichment.fix: Renamed the label to "storage_cluster_id" for the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, making it unique and clearly indicating the etcd storage cluster identifier.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting systems that scrape this metric must update their queries to use the new label name, but will benefit from reduced label collisions and clearer metric semantics.

apiChange.description:
Improved scheduling performance when many nodes, and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset)
  For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
apiChange.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: Scheduling suffered performance penalties in large clusters when the prefilter phase narrowed the candidate node list to only a few nodes (e.g., DaemonSet pods). Additionally, out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins could not rely on a clear meaning for missing entries in the NodeToStatusMap, leading to ambiguous plugin behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many nodes where prefilter filters to a tiny node set (e.g., DaemonSet pods) and developers of out‑of‑tree PostFilter scheduler plugins.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now short‑circuits and skips unnecessary work when prefilter returns 1‑2 nodes, greatly speeding up scheduling in such scenarios. The NodeToStatusMap contract is changed so that any node absent from the map is treated as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status, giving plugins a deterministic interpretation.
enrichment.impact: Large clusters (hundreds‑thousands of nodes) experience faster pod placement, especially for DaemonSet workloads. Plugin developers must update their PostFilter implementations to handle the new default status for missing nodes.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.)
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the Kubernetes build process to use Go 1.21.10, replacing the previous Go version used for compilation.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries are built with a newer, patched Go compiler, bringing compiler security fixes, performance improvements, and better compatibility for future Go releases. This reduces the risk of compiler‑related vulnerabilities and ensures smoother upgrades.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; the release updates the build toolchain to Go 1.21.11.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) compiled into the release.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled using Go 1.21.11, bringing in upstream bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements from the Go runtime.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that clusters benefit from the latest Go runtime stability and security updates, reduces risk of runtime‑level bugs, and aligns the codebase with the supported Go version for future releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Emition of RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events has been removed from stateful set lifecycle.
bugOrRegression.author: atiratree

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet controller emitted RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events during pod recreation, leading to noisy or misleading event streams for users who monitor StatefulSet events.
enrichment.affected: Users and automation that watch StatefulSet events for pod recreation (e.g., monitoring, CI/CD pipelines) will no longer receive RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events.
enrichment.fix: The emission of the RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events has been removed from the StatefulSet lifecycle, so these events will no longer be generated.
enrichment.impact: Event‑based tooling, alerts, or scripts that relied on these events must be updated to stop expecting them. The change reduces event noise and prevents confusion about pod recreation status.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed PersistentolumeLabel providing wrong topology labels to Azure Disk PersistentVolumes when the external Azure cloud provider is used.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: PersistentVolumeLabel generated incorrect topology labels for Azure Disk PersistentVolumes when using the external Azure cloud provider, causing pods to be scheduled to nodes without access to the volume.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Azure Disk PersistentVolumes with the external Azure cloud provider; workloads that depend on correct volume topology for scheduling.
enrichment.fix: Updated the PersistentVolumeLabel logic to correctly derive and apply the Azure Disk topology labels, ensuring the volume's zone information matches the actual Azure Disk location.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on Azure Disk PVs will now be scheduled to appropriate nodes, preventing bind failures and improving reliability for workloads using Azure Disk storage with the external cloud provider.

bugOrRegression.description: Improved scheduling latency when many gated pods
bugOrRegression.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: When a large number of gated pods are present, the scheduler experiences increased latency, delaying pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Users running workloads that create many gated pods (e.g., jobs that use scheduling gates or custom controllers) experienced slower scheduling.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code path handling gated pods was optimized, reducing the time spent processing them and improving overall scheduling latency.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with many gated pods will see faster pod scheduling, leading to quicker workload start‑up and better resource utilization.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.28 regression printing pods with invalid initContainer status
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes v1.28 a regression caused the kube-apiserver to incorrectly display pod information when an initContainer had an invalid status, leading to misleading pod status output.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 that have pods with initContainers in an invalid state; essentially any user querying pod status via kubectl or API.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver code was updated to correctly handle and print pods with initContainers that are in an invalid state, restoring accurate status reporting.
enrichment.impact: Users and cluster administrators see correct pod status for workloads with failing initContainers, improving troubleshooting and preventing misinterpretation of pod health.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-scheduler: fixes a 1.29.5 regression that can lead to a scheduler crash when processing pods with affinity that doesn't match a real/valid node
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.29.5 caused kube-scheduler to panic and crash when it processed pods whose node affinity rules referenced a node that does not exist or is not valid.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running 1.29.5 that have pods with nodeAffinity or related affinity rules pointing to non‑existent nodes could experience a scheduler crash, affecting all scheduling operations.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler's affinity handling code was corrected to properly validate node names and gracefully ignore or reject invalid affinity specifications instead of crashing.
enrichment.impact: Restores scheduler stability, preventing cluster-wide scheduling outages for workloads that use node affinity, and ensures pods continue to be scheduled normally.

bugOrRegression.description: Reduce critical section in watchcache to fix kube-apiserver scalability under heavy load of list requests
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver experienced reduced scalability and high latency when handling a large number of list requests because the watchcache held a large critical section, causing lock contention.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that generate heavy list traffic (e.g., controllers, dashboards, CI systems) suffered degraded API responsiveness; all clients of the kube-apiserver were affected.
enrichment.fix: The watchcache implementation was changed to shrink the critical section, lowering lock contention and allowing the API server to process list requests more efficiently under heavy load.
enrichment.impact: Improves API server throughput and latency for list‑heavy workloads, preventing the API server from becoming a bottleneck in large clusters and providing more stable performance during peak traffic.

securityFixes.title: Incorrect permissions on Windows containers logs
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes clusters with Windows nodes
where BUILTIN\Users may be able to read container logs and NT
AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users may be able to modify container logs.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.4
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes binaries were still being built with an older Go version, missing recent language security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All released Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kubelet, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.)
enrichment.fix: The build process was updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.4.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using official binaries benefit from the security and stability updates in Go 1.22.4, and the codebase stays compatible with future Go releases.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go toolchain, missing recent language security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl) and any clusters that run those binaries.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.22.5, updating the compiler and standard library for all components.
enrichment.impact: Clusters built from source now benefit from Go security fixes, runtime performance enhancements, and future compatibility, reducing risk of bugs introduced by an outdated toolchain.

bugOrRegression.description: Add `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` to default masked paths. It avoids the potential security risk that the ability to read these files may offer a power-based sidechannel attack against any workloads running on the same kernel.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Reading files under /sys/devices/virtual/powercap could be used for a power‑based side‑channel attack, allowing a malicious workload to infer information about co‑located workloads on the same kernel.
enrichment.affected: All pods and containers running on a node where the kubelet masks the powercap path; particularly relevant for multi‑tenant environments.
enrichment.fix: The path /sys/devices/virtual/powercap is now included in the kubelet's default masked paths, preventing containers from reading these files.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface for multi‑tenant clusters by blocking a potential side‑channel vector, improving overall node security for all workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Drop additional rule requirement (cronjobs/finalizers) in the roles who use kubectl create cronjobs to be backwards compatible
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kubectl create cronjobs required an extra RBAC rule for managing cronjob finalizers, causing users with roles that only permitted create on cronjobs to fail when using the command, breaking backward compatibility.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where users or service accounts had roles granting only "create" on cronjobs but not finalizer access, and attempted to use "kubectl create cronjob".
enrichment.fix: The additional finalizer rule requirement is removed; kubectl now only needs the create permission on cronjobs, restoring the original RBAC expectations.
enrichment.impact: Users with minimal RBAC roles can again create cronjobs with kubectl without granting unnecessary finalizer permissions, simplifying permission management and fixing automation scripts that relied on the prior behavior.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix a bug that Pods could stuck in the unschedulable pod pool 
  if they're rejected by PreEnqueue plugins that could change its result by a change in resources apart from Pods.
  DRA plugin is the only plugin that meets the criteria of the bug in in-tree, 
  and hence if you have `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature flag enabled, 
  your DRA Pods could be affected by this bug.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: Pods could remain indefinitely in the unschedulable pod pool when a PreEnqueue plugin (specifically the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) plugin) rejects them, and the scheduler does not re‑evaluate them after resource changes unrelated to the pod.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the DynamicResourceAllocation feature enabled; DRA workloads that were previously stuck in the unschedulable pool.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the scheduler’s handling of the unschedulable pod pool so that pods rejected by PreEnqueue plugins are re‑queued when relevant resources change, preventing them from getting stuck.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use the DynamicResourceAllocation feature can now be scheduled once the necessary resources become available, improving reliability for workloads that rely on DRA.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix endpoints status out-of-sync when the pod state changes rapidly
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: When pods transitioned state rapidly (e.g., during fast rollouts or burst creations), the Service Endpoints object could become out of sync with the actual pod readiness, causing stale or missing endpoints.
enrichment.affected: Users running Services that depend on accurate endpoint lists, especially during rapid pod creation/deletion such as rolling updates or burst workloads.
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic to correctly update Endpoints status in response to rapid pod state changes, ensuring the Service controller synchronizes endpoint lists promptly.
enrichment.impact: Services now reliably reflect the current set of ready pods, preventing traffic from being sent to terminated or not-yet-ready pods and reducing connection errors during fast pod churn.

bugOrRegression.description:
For statically provisioned PVs, if its volume source is CSI type or it has migrated annotation, when it's deleted, the PersisentVolume controller won't changes its phase to the Failed state. 
  With this patch, the external provisioner can remove the finalizer in next reconcile loop. Unfortunately if the provious existing pv has the Failed state, this patch won't take effort. It requires users to remove finalizer.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Statically provisioned PersistentVolumes with a CSI volume source or the migrated annotation were not having their phase set to Failed when deleted, preventing the PersistentVolume controller from removing the finalizer and causing the PV to become stuck.
enrichment.affected: Users with statically provisioned PVs that use CSI drivers or have the migrated annotation; clusters where such PVs are deleted.
enrichment.fix: The PV controller now sets the phase to Failed for such PVs during deletion, allowing the external provisioner to clear the finalizer in the next reconcile loop. Existing PVs already in Failed state still require manual finalizer removal.
enrichment.impact: Prevents PVs from lingering in a non‑deletable state, ensuring proper cleanup of storage resources and improving reliability for users relying on static CSI volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: do not exit with an error if the "super-admin.conf" cannot create a ClusterRoleBinding for the "cluster-admin" user, due to the ClusterRoleBInding already existing.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm aborts with an error when creating the "cluster-admin" ClusterRoleBinding from super-admin.conf if the binding already exists, causing init/join to fail.
enrichment.affected: Operators using kubeadm to bootstrap or join a cluster where the "cluster-admin" ClusterRoleBinding may already be present.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now treats an existing ClusterRoleBinding as a non‑fatal condition and continues without exiting with an error.
enrichment.impact: Users can re‑run kubeadm init or join in environments where the cluster‑admin binding is pre‑created (e.g., after a failed run or custom RBAC setup) without the operation stopping unexpectedly.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: cji

enrichment.problem: Not specified – the release note provides no details about the change.
enrichment.affected: Not specified – no information about affected workloads, configurations, or environments is provided.
enrichment.fix: Not specified – without a description we cannot detail the implementation.
enrichment.impact: Not specified – the effect on users, workloads, or Windows nodes cannot be determined from the available information.

apiChange.description: Fixed a bug in the API server where empty collections of ValidatingAdmissionPolicies did not have an `items` field.
apiChange.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: When the API server returned an empty list of ValidatingAdmissionPolicies, the response omitted the `items` field, causing clients that expect an array to fail or misinterpret the result.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that queries the `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` list API (e.g., kubectl, CI pipelines, UI dashboards) was affected by the missing `items` field.
enrichment.fix: The API server now always includes an `items` array in the response, even when the collection is empty, conforming to the standard list schema.
enrichment.impact: Clients, scripts, and kubectl commands that list ValidatingAdmissionPolicies can reliably parse the response without special‑case handling, preventing errors and improving stability of admission policy management.

apiChange.description: Use omitempty for optional Job Pod Failure Policy fields
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Optional fields in the Job spec's PodFailurePolicy were always serialized in API objects even when unset, resulting in unnecessary empty fields being sent to the API server and potentially causing compatibility or validation issues.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing Jobs that include a PodFailurePolicy with optional fields left unset, as well as any tooling that consumes Job objects.
enrichment.fix: Added `omitempty` tags to the optional Job PodFailurePolicy fields so they are omitted from the serialized representation when they are not set.
enrichment.impact: API objects for Jobs are now cleaner and smaller, avoiding extraneous empty fields. This improves client compatibility and reduces API payload size without changing Job behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix the bug where PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When a pod reached a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed), the PodIP field was temporarily removed from the pod's status, causing the IP to disappear for short periods.
enrichment.affected: Pods that quickly transition to a terminal state; any system or user process that queries a pod's IP after termination.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the pod termination handling so that the PodIP is retained in the pod status even after the pod becomes terminal, preventing its brief removal.
enrichment.impact: Components that inspect a pod's IP after it has finished (e.g., monitoring, logging, network policies) will now see a stable IP, eliminating errors and improving reliability of workloads that rely on the IP post‑completion.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that init containers with `Always` restartPolicy may not terminate gracefully if the pod hasn't initialized yet.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: Init containers with a restartPolicy of `Always` could fail to terminate gracefully when the pod had not yet completed its initialization phase.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use init containers with `restartPolicy: Always` before the pod has finished its initialization.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a correction so that init containers respect graceful termination even when the pod is still initializing, ensuring the `Always` restartPolicy behaves correctly.
enrichment.impact: Prevents init containers from hanging or being force‑killed, improving pod lifecycle reliability and preventing delays or resource leaks in workloads that rely on init containers with `Always` restartPolicy.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression watching a single namespace via the deprecated /api/v1/watch/namespaces/$name endpoint where watch events were not delivered after the watch was established
bugOrRegression.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.27 and later, watches on a single namespace using the deprecated endpoint /api/v1/watch/namespaces/$name stopped delivering events after the watch was established, breaking functionality that relied on that API.
enrichment.affected: Clients (e.g., controllers, operators, scripts) that watch a single namespace via the deprecated /api/v1/watch/namespaces/$name endpoint.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver was updated to correctly handle the deprecated namespace watch endpoint, ensuring that watch events are delivered continuously after the watch is set up.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable watch behavior for clients that still use the deprecated single‑namespace watch API, preventing missed events and allowing existing controllers, operators, and scripts to function correctly.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a potential crash serving CustomResourceDefinitions that combine an invalid schema and CEL validation rules.
bugOrRegression.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: Kube-apiserver could crash when serving CustomResourceDefinitions that contain both an invalid OpenAPI schema and CEL validation rules, causing a potential cluster-wide outage.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CustomResourceDefinitions that define an invalid OpenAPI schema together with CEL validation expressions. The issue affected the kube-apiserver's ability to serve those resources.
enrichment.fix: Added validation in the apiserver to detect and reject the combination of an invalid schema with CEL rules, preventing the crash and allowing the API server to continue serving other resources.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unexpected apiserver crashes, ensuring stability for clusters that use CRDs with CEL validation. Users no longer risk a full API outage due to malformed CRDs.

bugOrRegression.description: Mount-utils: treat syscall.ENODEV as corrupted mount
bugOrRegression.author: dobsonj

enrichment.problem: Mount-utils did not treat the ENODEV error (no such device) as indicating a corrupted mount, leading to situations where a pod's volume mount could be left in a bad state and cause pod start failures.
enrichment.affected: Pods that rely on volume mounts, especially when underlying devices disappear or become unavailable, causing mount operations to succeed superficially but actually be corrupted.
enrichment.fix: The mount-utils library was updated to recognize syscall.ENODEV as a sign of a corrupted mount and handle it accordingly (cleanup/retry), ensuring the mount is correctly reported as failed.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of volume mounting for pods, reducing mount-related failures and preventing pods from being stuck with unusable mounts.

bugOrRegression.description: StatefulSet autodelete will respect controlling owners on PVC claims as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4375
bugOrRegression.author: mattcary

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet's autodelete feature deleted PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) without checking their controlling owner references, causing unintended PVC deletion when other resources owned the PVC.
enrichment.affected: Users who delete StatefulSets that have PVCs which are also owned by other controllers or resources could lose data. Workloads sharing PVCs are now protected.
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSet controller was updated to respect controlling owner references on PVCs during autodelete, only deleting PVCs that are exclusively owned by the StatefulSet.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental data loss and ensures correct ownership semantics for PVCs used by StatefulSets, making deletions safer for workloads that share storage.

bugOrRegression.description: Stop using wmic on Windows to get uuid in the kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: The kubelet on Windows used the wmic command to retrieve the system UUID, which can fail or be unavailable on certain Windows versions, leading to node identity or registration issues.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running the kubelet, especially those where wmic is unavailable or unreliable.
enrichment.fix: The implementation was changed to stop using wmic for UUID retrieval on Windows, opting for a more reliable method.
enrichment.impact: Improves stability and reliability of Windows nodes joining the cluster, preventing kubelet startup or node registration failures.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes build process was using an older Go compiler version, which could miss security updates, performance improvements, and compatibility fixes provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: Developers and organizations building Kubernetes binaries from source, as well as CI systems that compile the project.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.22.6, aligning the project with a recent, supported Go release.
enrichment.impact: All users who compile Kubernetes from source—including distribution maintainers, CI/CD pipelines, and developers—receive the benefits of Go's latest security patches, bug fixes, and performance enhancements, reducing potential downstream issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a scheduler preemption issue where the victim pod was not deleted due to incorrect status patching. This issue occurred when the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes in their status, causing the preemption to fail entirely.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: During scheduler preemption, the victim pod was not deleted because the status patch applied the wrong QoS class. When the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes, the preemption process failed completely, preventing high‑priority pods from being scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube‑scheduler preemption, especially when preemptor and victim pods belong to different QoS classes. Affected workloads include any pods that may be preempted to make room for higher‑priority pods.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s preemption logic was updated to correctly patch the victim pod’s status regardless of QoS class differences, ensuring the victim pod is properly deleted and preemption can proceed.
enrichment.impact: Restores correct preemption behavior, allowing high‑priority pods to preempt lower‑priority ones. This prevents scheduling dead‑locks and reduces potential service disruptions for workloads that rely on preemption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix race condition in kube-proxy initialization that could blackhole UDP traffic to service VIP.
bugOrRegression.author: wedaly

enrichment.problem: A race condition during kube-proxy startup could leave the iptables/ipvs rules for a Service VIP incomplete, causing UDP packets to be silently dropped (blackholed).
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy for Service routing with UDP traffic; any pod that accesses a Service VIP over UDP could see dropped packets.
enrichment.fix: The initialization sequence in kube-proxy was reworked to serialize rule creation, eliminating the race and ensuring UDP traffic is correctly programmed to the service IP.
enrichment.impact: UDP-based services (e.g., DNS, SIP, custom protocols) will no longer experience intermittent connectivity loss, improving reliability of networking for workloads that depend on UDP.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: Init containers could fail to start when the container runtime experienced a temporary failure, causing the pod to be unable to progress.
enrichment.affected: Any pod using init containers, across all workloads, could be impacted when a node’s container runtime temporarily fails.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now properly retries and handles transient container runtime errors when launching init containers, preventing premature pod failure.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers will start reliably even if the container runtime briefly hiccups, reducing pod startup failures and improving overall workload stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a regression in 1.29+ default configurations, where regular init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in the default configurations for Kubernetes 1.29+ caused regular init containers to fail to start because of a temporary container runtime failure.
enrichment.affected: Pods with init containers could fail to start, affecting any workloads that depend on them.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected so that init containers start normally under the default configuration, eliminating the spurious runtime failure.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers can now start reliably, preventing startup delays or failures for workloads that use init containers.

bugOrRegression.description: Terminated Pods on a node will not be re-admitted on kubelet restart. This fixes the problem of Completed Pods awaiting for the finalizer marked as Failed after the kubelet restart.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: After a kubelet restart, pods that were already terminated (e.g., Completed) were re‑admitted to the node and marked as Failed while waiting for their finalizers, causing pod lifecycle stalling.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that rely on pod termination finalizers (e.g., Jobs, CronJobs) running on nodes where the kubelet restarts.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now skips re‑admitting terminated pods on restart, so Completed pods are no longer marked Failed and can finish their finalizer processing correctly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that batch and job workloads do not end up with stuck or incorrectly failed pods after a node kubelet restart, improving reliability of pod termination and finalizer handling.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.7
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go toolchain, which could miss security patches, bug fixes, and compatibility improvements present in newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: Anyone who builds Kubernetes from source (e.g., developers, CI systems, Linux distribution packagers). End‑users of pre‑built binaries are not directly affected.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.22.7, ensuring that all Kubernetes components are compiled with the latest supported Go version.
enrichment.impact: Developers, CI pipelines, and downstream distributors now get binaries built with a more secure and up‑to‑date compiler, reducing the risk of compiler‑related bugs and improving future compatibility.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.8
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which may miss recent compiler improvements and security patches.
enrichment.affected: Users building Kubernetes from source and any deployments using those binaries. All components are recompiled with the new Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.8.
enrichment.impact: All components built from source (kube-apiserver, kubelet, controller-manager, scheduler, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) benefit from the latest Go language and runtime updates, including security fixes, performance improvements, and better future compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Ensure daemonset controller to count old unhealthy pods towards max unavailable budget
bugOrRegression.author: ncdc

enrichment.problem: During DaemonSet updates, the controller did not include already‑unhealthy pods from previous revisions when calculating the maxUnavailable budget, allowing more pods to be unavailable than intended.
enrichment.affected: Users running DaemonSets that specify maxUnavailable (or rely on its default) and have pods that may become unhealthy during updates.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller now counts old unhealthy pods toward the maxUnavailable budget, ensuring the update respects the configured unavailability limit.
enrichment.impact: Updates to DaemonSets respect the defined maxUnavailable limit, reducing unexpected downtime and improving reliability for workloads that depend on DaemonSets.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: The endpoints controller in kube-controller-manager did not trigger a reconciliation of the Endpoint object after the endpoint list was truncated when it exceeded 1000 addresses, leaving the Endpoint resource stale.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running services that generate more than 1000 endpoint addresses. Users relying on large Service/Endpoint sets could see stale endpoints and broken traffic routing.
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic to ensure the Endpoint object is reconciled after truncation, guaranteeing that the Endpoint resource is updated correctly even when the address list is limited to 1000 entries.
enrichment.impact: Services with more than 1000 endpoints (e.g., large headless services or high‑scale workloads) will now have accurate Endpoint objects, preventing traffic from being directed to removed pods and avoiding connectivity issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
bugOrRegression.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: A memory leak was introduced in the default tracing configuration of kubelet and kube-apiserver in Kubernetes 1.29, causing memory usage to grow over time.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the default 1.29 tracing configuration on both the node (kubelet) and control‑plane (kube-apiserver) components.
enrichment.fix: The leak was corrected in both kubelet and kube-apiserver code, ensuring that tracing data is properly cleaned up and memory is released.
enrichment.impact: Preventing uncontrolled memory growth stabilizes node and control‑plane processes, avoiding potential OOM crashes and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression introduced in 1.29 where conntrack entries for UDP connections
  to deleted pods did not get cleaned up correctly, which could (among other things)
  cause DNS problems when DNS pods were restarted.
bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.29 caused conntrack entries for UDP connections to pods that had been deleted to remain in the kernel connection tracking table. Stale entries prevented proper cleanup of UDP traffic, leading to DNS resolution failures when DNS pods were restarted.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use UDP (especially DNS pods) and any workloads that rely on DNS resolution were impacted by intermittent connectivity failures after DNS pod restarts.
enrichment.fix: The cleanup logic for conntrack entries was corrected so that UDP connections to deleted pods are now removed promptly, preventing leftover state from persisting after pod deletion.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable DNS service and overall UDP connectivity after pod restarts, preventing cluster‑wide name resolution issues and improving network stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix wrong member list reported when removing an etcd member
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When removing an etcd member using kubeadm, the command reported an incorrect list of etcd members, causing confusion about the current cluster state.
enrichment.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm where an etcd member is removed; cluster administrators using kubeadm to manage etcd members.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now correctly updates and displays the etcd member list after a member removal operation.
enrichment.impact: Administrators get accurate visibility of etcd membership, preventing mis‑interpretation and potential mis‑management of the etcd cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeadm join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When adding new control‑plane nodes with `kubeadm join`, the command could add an etcd member even if the member’s URL was already present, leading to duplicate entries and join failures. Likewise, `kubeadm reset` attempted to delete an etcd member without checking if the member ID existed, causing unnecessary errors.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where control‑plane nodes are added or removed using `kubeadm join` and `kubeadm reset`, especially HA setups with stacked etcd.
enrichment.fix: Added idempotent checks: `kubeadm join` now adds an etcd member only if its URL is not already in the cluster’s member list, and `kubeadm reset` removes an etcd member only when the corresponding ID is present.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable addition and removal of control‑plane nodes with kubeadm, preventing join errors and spurious reset failures. This improves cluster stability for users managing HA control‑plane clusters via kubeadm.

bugOrRegression.description:
The scheduling queue didn't notice any extenders' failures, it could miss some cluster events,
  and it could end up Pods rejected by Extenders stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min in the worst-case scenario.
  Now, the scheduling queue notices extenders' failures and requeue Pods rejected by Extenders appropriately.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The scheduling queue failed to detect failures from scheduler extenders, causing it to miss related cluster events and leaving pods rejected by extenders in the unschedulable pod pool for up to five minutes.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that is scheduled through a scheduler extender could be delayed or remain unschedulable when the extender fails.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now monitors extender failures and requeues pods rejected by extenders, ensuring they are retried promptly.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on scheduler extenders are no longer stuck in an unschedulable state, reducing scheduling latency and improving overall cluster reliability.

other.description: Kubeadm: removed `socat` and `ebtables` from kubeadm preflight checks
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: kubeadm preflight checks required the presence of `socat` and `ebtables` binaries even when they were not needed, causing init/join to fail on minimal systems.
enrichment.affected: Operators using kubeadm on nodes that lack `socat` or `ebtables`, especially those using minimal or custom OS images.
enrichment.fix: The preflight validation no longer checks for `socat` and `ebtables`. These tools are only required later if a networking configuration needs them.
enrichment.impact: Users can run kubeadm on slimmer images or environments without installing these utilities, reducing unnecessary setup steps and false‑positive failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug when the hostname label of a node does not match the node name, pods bound to a PV with nodeAffinity using the hostname may be scheduled to the wrong node or experience scheduling failures.
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: When a node’s `kubernetes.io/hostname` label does not match the node’s actual name, PersistentVolumes that use nodeAffinity on the hostname label cause pods to be scheduled to the wrong node or to fail scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Workloads using PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity that reference the node’s hostname label, especially in clusters where the hostname label differs from the node name.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s node‑affinity logic for PersistentVolumes now correctly handles mismatched hostname labels, ensuring pods are placed on the intended node even when the label and node name differ.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on PV nodeAffinity based on the hostname will be scheduled reliably, preventing mis‑placements and scheduling failures for affected workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a suboptimal scheduler preemption behavior where potential preemption victims were violating Pod Disruption Budgets.
bugOrRegression.author: NoicFank

enrichment.problem: The scheduler’s preemption logic could select pods for eviction that would violate existing Pod Disruption Budgets, causing unintended disruptions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with Pod Disruption Budgets enabled and using preemption for high‑priority pods were at risk of exceeding the allowed disruption limits.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler preemption now checks Pod Disruption Budgets and excludes victims that would breach them, selecting only permissible pods for preemption.
enrichment.impact: Ensures high‑priority pods can preempt lower‑priority ones without violating availability guarantees, improving reliability for workloads that define PDBs.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go version, missing out on recent language improvements, security patches, and performance fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source, including kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, and related binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to use Go 1.22.9 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components now benefit from the latest Go runtime security updates and performance enhancements, improving overall stability and future compatibility for users and developers.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix kubelet on Windows fails if a pod has SecurityContext with RunAsUser
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Kubelet on Windows crashes or fails to start pods that specify a SecurityContext with a RunAsUser value.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes with kubelet and deploying pods that set `securityContext.runAsUser`.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet Windows implementation was updated to properly handle the RunAsUser field in a pod's SecurityContext, allowing such pods to be created and run without error.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that need to run under a specific user ID can now be scheduled and run correctly, eliminating pod creation failures on Windows nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a storage bug around multipath. iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices attached to nodes via multipath now resolve correctly if partitioned.
bugOrRegression.author: RomanBednar

enrichment.problem: Multipath-attached iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices that were partitioned were not resolved correctly on nodes, causing volume attachment failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage presented via multipath on nodes, especially when the devices are partitioned.
enrichment.fix: The multipath handling logic was fixed so that partitioned iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices are resolved properly during attachment.
enrichment.impact: Nodes can now successfully discover and attach partitioned multipath storage devices, preventing pod mount errors and improving reliability of storage workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a panic in kube-controller-manager handling StatefulSet objects when revisionHistoryLimit is negative
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager would panic and crash when it processed a StatefulSet that had a negative revisionHistoryLimit value.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with StatefulSet resources where the spec.revisionHistoryLimit was set to a negative number, which could cause the controller manager to panic and restart.
enrichment.fix: Added validation in the StatefulSet controller to detect a negative revisionHistoryLimit and handle it safely instead of dereferencing a nil pointer, preventing the panic.
enrichment.impact: Prevents the controller-manager from crashing, keeping StatefulSet management functional and maintaining overall control‑plane stability for clusters that had the mis‑configured field.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: Fix the volume manager didn't check the device mount state in the actual state of the world before marking the volume as detached. It may cause a pod to be stuck in the Terminating state due to the above issue when it was deleted.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The kubelet volume manager could mark a volume as detached without first checking the device’s mount state in the actual state of the world. When a pod using that volume was deleted, the pod could become stuck in the Terminating phase.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use attached volumes and are being deleted; the kubelet on the node hosting those pods.
enrichment.fix: The volume manager now validates the mount state of the block device before marking the volume detached, ensuring the pod cleanup proceeds correctly.
enrichment.impact: Pods that are deleted will no longer remain indefinitely in the Terminating state, improving reliability of workload termination and freeing resources promptly.
